Intra-articular injection of corticosteroid resulted in a significant decrease in the enlarged ultrasonographic distance, in joints both with and without synovial fluid. Joints not treated with steroid did not show any change. It is concluded that both joint effusion and synovitis without effusion can increase the anechogenic distance between the bone and the joint capsule.

topic: Greater trochanteric pain syndrome: sonographic findings and rarity of primary bursitis
title: Sonography of greater trochanteric pain syndrome and the rarity of primary bursitis.
key_points: Retrospective review of musculoskeletal ultrasound in 877 patients with greater trochanteric pain syndrome over a 6-year period.
700 patients (79.8%) did not have bursitis on ultrasound; 177 (20.2%) had trochanteric bursitis.
Gluteal tendinosis was found in 438 (49.9%), gluteal tendon tears in 4 (0.5%) and a thickened iliotibial band in 250 (28.5%).
GTPS is usually caused by some combination of gluteus medius/minimus tendon and iliotibial band pathology; bursitis is present in only a minority.
key_points_pt: Revisão retrospetiva de ecografias musculoesqueléticas em 877 doentes com síndrome dolorosa do grande trocânter ao longo de 6 anos.
700 doentes (79,8%) não tinham bursite na ecografia; 177 (20,2%) tinham bursite trocantérica.
Encontrou-se tendinose glútea em 438 (49,9%), rotura dos tendões glúteos em 4 (0,5%) e espessamento da banda iliotibial em 250 (28,5%).
A síndrome dolorosa do grande trocânter deve-se habitualmente a uma combinação de patologia dos tendões do glúteo médio/mínimo e da banda iliotibial; a bursite está presente apenas numa minoria.
abstract_excerpt: RESULTS: The final study population consisted of 877 unique patients: 602 women, 275 men; average age, 54 years; and age range, 15-87 years). Of the 877 patients with greater trochanteric pain, 700 (79.8%) did not have bursitis on ultrasound. A minority of patients (177, 20.2%) had trochanteric bursitis. Of the 877 patients with greater trochanteric pain, 438 (49.9%) had gluteal tendinosis, four (0.5%) had gluteal tendon tears, and 250 (28.5%) had a thickened iliotibial band. CONCLUSION: The cause of greater trochanteric pain syndrome is usually some combination of pathology involving the gluteus medius and gluteus minimus tendons as well as the iliotibial band. Bursitis is present in only the minority of patients.

topic: Greater trochanteric pain syndrome: MRI and ultrasound accuracy for gluteal tendon tears (systematic review)
title: The diagnostic accuracy of magnetic resonance imaging and ultrasonography in gluteal tendon tears--a systematic review.
key_points: 7 studies compared MRI or ultrasound with surgical findings in persistent lateral hip pain/GTPS.
MRI: sensitivity 33-100%, specificity 92-100%, PPV 71-100%, NPV 50%; false positives were common.
High MRI signal located superior to the trochanter had a stronger association with tears.
Ultrasound: sensitivity 79-100% and PPV 95-100%; may prove the investigation of choice, although it requires a skilled practitioner; the amount and quality of the literature are limited.
key_points_pt: 7 estudos compararam RM ou ecografia com os achados cirúrgicos em dor lateral persistente da anca/síndrome dolorosa do grande trocânter.
RM: sensibilidade 33-100%, especificidade 92-100%, VPP 71-100%, VPN 50%; os falsos positivos foram frequentes.
O hipersinal em RM localizado acima do trocânter associou-se mais fortemente a rotura.
Ecografia: sensibilidade 79-100% e VPP 95-100%; poderá vir a ser o exame de eleição, embora exija um operador experiente; a quantidade e a qualidade da literatura são limitadas.
abstract_excerpt: 7 studies met the inclusion criteria, comparing either imaging modality with a reference standard of surgical findings. [...] MRI had sensitivity of 33-100%, specificity of 92-100%, positive predictive value of 71-100% and negative predictive value of 50%. False-positives were common. High signal located superior to the trochanter had a stronger association with tears. Ultrasonography had a sensitivity of 79-100% and positive predictive value of 95-100%. The amount and quality of literature on the subject is limited and further well-designed studies are required to establish the optimum diagnostic strategy in this condition. Ultrasonography may prove to be the investigation of choice, despite requiring a skilled practitioner.

topic: Bone stress injury: original Fredericson MRI grading of tibial stress reaction in runners
title: Tibial stress reaction in runners. Correlation of clinical symptoms and scintigraphy with a new magnetic resonance imaging grading system.
journal: The American Journal of Sports Medicine
key_points: MRI suggests a progression of tibial stress injury: periosteal edema, then progressive marrow involvement, and ultimately frank cortical stress fracture.

In 14 runners (18 symptomatic legs), MRI findings correlated with an established technetium bone scan grading system in 14 of 18 legs and more precisely defined anatomic location and extent of injury.
Pain with daily ambulation, localized tibial tenderness and pain with direct or indirect percussion correlated with more severe tibial stress injuries.
When clinically warranted, authors recommend MRI over bone scan for grading tibial stress lesions in runners, citing better correlation of bone involvement with symptoms and no ionizing radiation.
key_points_pt: A RM sugere uma progressão da lesão de stress da tíbia: edema periosteal, depois envolvimento medular progressivo e, por fim, fratura de stress cortical franca.

Em 14 corredores (18 membros sintomáticos), os achados de RM correlacionaram-se com uma graduação cintigráfica com tecnécio estabelecida em 14 de 18 membros e definiram com mais precisão a localização anatómica e a extensão da lesão.
Dor na marcha diária, dor localizada à palpação da tíbia e dor à percussão direta ou indireta correlacionaram-se com lesões de stress tibiais mais graves.

Quando clinicamente justificado, os autores recomendam a RM em vez da cintigrafia para graduar as lesões de stress tibiais em corredores, pela melhor correlação do envolvimento ósseo com os sintomas e pela ausência de radiação ionizante.
abstract_excerpt: Our work using magnetic resonance imaging suggests that a progression of injury can be identified, starting with periosteal edema, then progressive marrow involvement, and ultimately frank cortical stress fracture. Fourteen runners, with a total of 18 symptomatic legs, were evaluated and, within 10 days, referred for radiographs, a technetium bone scan, and a magnetic resonance imaging scan. In 14 of the 18 symptomatic legs, magnetic resonance imaging findings correlated with an established technetium bone scan grading system and more precisely defined the anatomic location and extent of injury. We identified clinical symptoms, such as pain with daily ambulation and physical examination findings, including localized tibial tenderness and pain with direct or indirect percussion, that correlated with more severe tibial stress injuries. When clinically warranted, we recommend magnetic resonance imaging over bone scan for grading of tibial stress lesions in runners. Magnetic resonance imaging is more accurate in correlating the degree of bone involvement with clinical symptoms, allowing for more accurate recommendations for rehabilitation and return to impact activity. Additional advantages of magnetic resonance imaging include lack of exposure to ionizing radiation and significantly less imaging time than three-phase bone scintigraphy.

topic: Bone stress injury: validation of the Fredericson MRI classification for tibial stress injuries
title: Validation of MRI classification system for tibial stress injuries.
key_points: 142 tibial stress injuries, retrospectively reviewed in consensus by two musculoskeletal radiologists, graded with the Fredericson system: grade 1 periosteal edema only; grade 2 bone marrow edema on T2-weighted images; grade 3 bone marrow edema on T1- and T2-weighted images; grade 4a multiple focal areas of intracortical signal abnormality; grade 4b linear areas of intracortical signal abnormality.
Grade 4b injuries had significantly more severe edema and longer time to return to sports, and grade 1 injuries less severe edema and shorter time, than grades 2, 3 and 4a (p < 0.002).
Grades 2, 3 and 4a did not differ significantly in periosteal/marrow edema or time to return to sports (p = 0.06-0.79).
Authors suggest combining grades 2, 3 and 4a into a single category (abbreviated Fredericson classification).
key_points_pt: 142 lesões de stress da tíbia, revistas retrospetivamente em consenso por dois radiologistas musculoesqueléticos, graduadas pelo sistema de Fredericson: grau 1 apenas edema periosteal; grau 2 edema da medula óssea em T2; grau 3 edema da medula óssea em T1 e T2; grau 4a múltiplas áreas focais de alteração de sinal intracortical; grau 4b áreas lineares de alteração de sinal intracortical.

As lesões de grau 4b tiveram edema significativamente mais grave e maior tempo até ao regresso ao desporto, e as de grau 1 edema menos grave e menor tempo, em comparação com os graus 2, 3 e 4a (p < 0,002).
Os graus 2, 3 e 4a não diferiram significativamente no edema periosteal/medular nem no tempo até ao regresso ao desporto (p = 0,06-0,79).
Os autores sugerem agrupar os graus 2, 3 e 4a numa única categoria (classificação de Fredericson abreviada).
abstract_excerpt: Two musculoskeletal radiologists retrospectively reviewed in consensus the MR findings of 142 tibial stress injuries to quantify the degree of periosteal and bone marrow edema and grade the injuries using the Fredericson classification system (grade 1 = periosteal edema only, grade 2 = bone marrow edema visible on T2-weighted images, grade 3 = bone marrow edema visible on T1-weighted and T2-weighted images, grade 4a = multiple focal areas of intracortical signal abnormality, and grade 4b = linear areas of intracortical signal abnormality). [...] RESULTS: Grade 4b injuries had significantly (p < 0.002) more severe and grade 1 injuries less severe periosteal and bone marrow edema than grades 2, 3, and 4a injuries. Grade 4b injuries had significantly (p < 0.002) longer time and grade 1 injuries shorter time to return to sports activity than grades 2, 3, and 4a injuries. There was no significant difference (p = 0.06-0.79) among grades 2, 3, and 4a injuries in the degree of periosteal and bone marrow edema and the time to return to sports activity. CONCLUSION: Grades 2, 3, and 4a stress injuries had similar degrees of periosteal and bone marrow edema and similar time to return to sports activity, which suggests that these three grades can be combined into a single category in an abbreviated Fredericson classification system.

topic: Lower extremity stress fractures: diagnostic accuracy of radiography, MRI, CT, scintigraphy and ultrasound (systematic review)
title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Various Imaging Modalities for Suspected Lower Extremity Stress Fractures: A Systematic Review With Evidence-Based Recommendations for Clinical Practice.
journal: The American Journal of Sports Medicine
key_points: Conventional radiography: sensitivity 12% to 56%, specificity 88% to 96%; radiographs are likely to be false negative at initial presentation, particularly in early stages, and in some cases may not reveal an existing stress fracture at any time.
MRI: sensitivity 68% to 99%, specificity 4% to 97%; identified by the authors as the most sensitive and specific imaging test for lower extremity stress fractures.
Ultrasound: sensitivity 43% to 99%, specificity 13% to 79%; CT: sensitivity 32% to 38%, specificity 88% to 98%; nuclear scintigraphy: sensitivity 50% to 97%, specificity 33% to 98%.
When MRI is available, nuclear scintigraphy is not recommended because of its low specificity, high dose of ionizing radiation and other limitations.
key_points_pt: Radiografia convencional: sensibilidade 12% a 56%, especificidade 88% a 96%; a radiografia tende a ser falsamente negativa na apresentação inicial, sobretudo nas fases precoces, e em alguns casos pode nunca revelar uma fratura de stress existente.
RM: sensibilidade 68% a 99%, especificidade 4% a 97%; identificada pelos autores como o exame de imagem mais sensível e específico para fraturas de stress do membro inferior.
Ecografia: sensibilidade 43% a 99%, especificidade 13% a 79%; TC: sensibilidade 32% a 38%, especificidade 88% a 98%; cintigrafia: sensibilidade 50% a 97%, especificidade 33% a 98%.
Quando a RM está disponível, a cintigrafia não é recomendada pela baixa especificidade, elevada dose de radiação ionizante e outras limitações.
abstract_excerpt: RESULTS: Reported sensitivity and specificity (95% CI) were as follows: For conventional radiography, sensitivity ranged from 12% (0%-29%) to 56% (39%-72%) and specificity ranged from 88% (55%-100%) to 96% (87%-100%). For nuclear scintigraphy (NS), sensitivity ranged from 50% (23%-77%) to 97% (90%-100%) and specificity from 33% (12%-53%) to 98% (93%-100%). For magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), sensitivity ranged from 68% (45%-90%) to 99% (95%-100%) and specificity from 4% (0%-11%) to 97% (88%-100%). For computed tomography, sensitivity ranged from 32% (8%-57%) to 38% (16%-59%) and specificity from 88% (55%-100%) to 98% (91%-100%). For ultrasound, sensitivity ranged from 43% (26%-61%) to 99% (95%-100%) and specificity from 13% (0%-45%) to 79% (61%-96%). CONCLUSION: MRI was identified as the most sensitive and specific imaging test for diagnosing stress fractures of the lower extremity. When MRI is available, NS is not recommended because of its low specificity, high dosage of ionizing radiation, and other limitations. Conventional radiographs are likely to result in false negatives upon initial presentation, particularly in the early stages of stress fracture, and in some cases may not reveal an existing stress fracture at any time.

topic: Interventional sports medicine: ultrasound-guided vs landmark-guided injections (AMSSM position statement)
title: American Medical Society for Sports Medicine (AMSSM) position statement: interventional musculoskeletal ultrasound in sports medicine.
key_points: Position statement based on a systematic review of the accuracy, efficacy and cost-effectiveness of ultrasound-guided injections in major, intermediate and small joints and soft tissues.
Ultrasound-guided injections are more accurate than landmark-guided injections (SORT evidence rating A; strong evidence).
Ultrasound-guided injections are more efficacious (SORT B; moderate evidence) and more cost-effective (SORT B; described as preliminary evidence) than landmark-guided injections.
Ultrasound guidance is required to perform many new procedures (SORT C).
key_points_pt: Tomada de posição baseada numa revisão sistemática da exatidão, eficácia e custo-efetividade das infiltrações ecoguiadas em articulações grandes, intermédias e pequenas e em partes moles.
As infiltrações ecoguiadas são mais exatas do que as guiadas por referências anatómicas (nível de evidência SORT A; evidência forte).
As infiltrações ecoguiadas são mais eficazes (SORT B; evidência moderada) e mais custo-efetivas (SORT B; descrita como evidência preliminar) do que as guiadas por referências anatómicas.
A orientação ecográfica é necessária para realizar muitos procedimentos novos (SORT C).
abstract_excerpt: OBJECTIVE: Critically review the literature related to the accuracy, efficacy and cost-effectiveness of ultrasound-guided injections (USGIs) in major, intermediate and small joints; and soft tissues. DESIGN: Systematic review of the literature. RESULTS: USGIs are more accurate than landmark-guided injections (LMGIs; strength of recommendation taxonomy (SORT) Evidence Rating=A). USGIs are more efficacious than LMGIs (SORT Evidence Rating=B). USGIs are more cost-effective than LMGIs (SORT Evidence Rating=B). Ultrasound guidance is required to perform many new procedures (SORT Evidence Rating=C). CONCLUSIONS: The findings of this position statement indicate there is strong evidence that USGIs are more accurate than LMGI, moderate evidence that they are more efficacious and preliminary evidence that they are more cost-effective.

topic: AI-assisted fracture detection: diagnostic accuracy meta-analysis
authors: Kuo RYL, Harrison C, Curran TA, et al.
title: Artificial Intelligence in Fracture Detection: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
key_points: Systematic review including 42 studies (37 on radiographs, 5 on CT); 115 contingency tables from 32 of these studies (55 061 images) were meta-analysed.
Internal validation: pooled sensitivity 92% (95% CI: 88, 93) for AI vs 91% (95% CI: 85, 95) for clinicians; pooled specificity 91% (95% CI: 88, 93) for AI vs 92% (95% CI: 89, 92) for clinicians.

External validation: pooled sensitivity 91% (95% CI: 84, 95) for AI vs 94% (95% CI: 90, 96) for clinicians; specificity 91% (95% CI: 81, 95) vs 94% (95% CI: 91, 95); no statistically significant differences between AI and clinicians.

22 of 42 (52%) studies were judged at high risk of bias; meta-regression identified sources of heterogeneity including risk of bias and fracture type. The authors concluded that AI and clinicians had comparable reported performance and that AI holds promise as a diagnostic adjunct.
key_points_pt: Revisão sistemática que incluiu 42 estudos (37 com radiografias, 5 com TC); foram meta-analisadas 115 tabelas de contingência de 32 desses estudos (55 061 imagens).

Validação interna: sensibilidade agregada de 92% (IC 95%: 88–93) para a IA vs 91% (IC 95%: 85–95) para os clínicos; especificidade agregada de 91% (IC 95%: 88–93) para a IA vs 92% (IC 95%: 89–92) para os clínicos.

Validação externa: sensibilidade agregada de 91% (IC 95%: 84–95) para a IA vs 94% (IC 95%: 90–96) para os clínicos; especificidade de 91% (IC 95%: 81–95) vs 94% (IC 95%: 91–95); sem diferenças estatisticamente significativas entre a IA e os clínicos.

22 de 42 estudos (52%) apresentavam risco de viés elevado; a meta-regressão identificou fontes de heterogeneidade, incluindo o risco de viés e o tipo de fratura. Os autores concluíram que a IA e os clínicos tiveram desempenho relatado comparável e que a IA é promissora como adjuvante diagnóstico.
abstract_excerpt: Results Included for analysis were 42 studies, with 115 contingency tables extracted from 32 studies (55 061 images). Thirty-seven studies identified fractures on radiographs and five studies identified fractures on CT images. For internal validation test sets, the pooled sensitivity was 92% (95% CI: 88, 93) for AI and 91% (95% CI: 85, 95) for clinicians, and the pooled specificity was 91% (95% CI: 88, 93) for AI and 92% (95% CI: 89, 92) for clinicians. For external validation test sets, the pooled sensitivity was 91% (95% CI: 84, 95) for AI and 94% (95% CI: 90, 96) for clinicians, and the pooled specificity was 91% (95% CI: 81, 95) for AI and 94% (95% CI: 91, 95) for clinicians. There were no statistically significant differences between clinician and AI performance. There were 22 of 42 (52%) studies that were judged to have high risk of bias. Meta-regression identified multiple sources of heterogeneity in the data, including risk of bias and fracture type. Conclusion Artificial intelligence (AI) and clinicians had comparable reported diagnostic performance in fracture detection, suggesting that AI technology holds promise as a diagnostic adjunct in future clinical practice.

topic: AI assistance for radiographic fracture detection: multi-reader multi-case study
authors: Guermazi A, Tannoury C, Kompel AJ, et al.
title: Improving Radiographic Fracture Recognition Performance and Efficiency Using Artificial Intelligence
key_points: Retrospective multi-reader multi-case study on an external multicentre data set: 480 examinations (fracture prevalence set at 50%) across 8 body regions, read by 24 readers of different specialties with and without AI assistance.
Per-patient sensitivity was 10.4% higher with AI aid (95% CI: 6.9, 13.9; 75.2% vs 64.8%; P < .001).
Per-patient specificity with AI aid was 95.6% vs 90.6% without (difference +5.0%, 95% CI: +2.0, +8.0; noninferior), and AI shortened average reading time by 6.3 seconds per examination.

The sensitivity gain was significant in all regions (+8.0% to +16.2%) except shoulder/clavicle (+4.2%) and spine (+2.6%). Several co-authors were affiliated with Gleamer, the developer of the AI software evaluated (vendor-affiliated study).
key_points_pt: Estudo retrospetivo multileitor e multicaso num conjunto de dados multicêntrico externo: 480 exames (prevalência de fratura fixada em 50%) em 8 regiões anatómicas, lidos por 24 leitores de diferentes especialidades com e sem apoio de IA.
A sensibilidade por doente foi 10,4% superior com apoio de IA (IC 95%: 6,9–13,9; 75,2% vs 64,8%; P < 0,001).
A especificidade por doente com apoio de IA foi de 95,6% vs 90,6% sem IA (diferença +5,0%, IC 95%: +2,0 a +8,0; não inferior), e a IA reduziu o tempo médio de leitura em 6,3 segundos por exame.

O ganho de sensibilidade foi significativo em todas as regiões (+8,0% a +16,2%), exceto ombro/clavícula (+4,2%) e coluna (+2,6%). Vários coautores estavam afiliados à Gleamer, a empresa que desenvolveu o software de IA avaliado (estudo com ligação ao fabricante).
abstract_excerpt: This retrospective diagnostic study used the multi-reader, multi-case methodology based on an external multicenter data set of 480 examinations with at least 60 examinations per body region (foot and ankle, knee and leg, hip and pelvis, hand and wrist, elbow and arm, shoulder and clavicle, rib cage, and thoracolumbar spine) between July 2020 and January 2021. Fracture prevalence was set at 50%. [...] Twenty-four readers (radiologists, orthopedists, emergency physicians, physician assistants, rheumatologists, family physicians) were presented the whole validation data set (n = 480), with and without AI assistance, with a 1-month minimum washout period. [...] The sensitivity per patient was 10.4% higher (95% CI: 6.9, 13.9; P < .001 for superiority) with AI aid (4331 of 5760 readings, 75.2%) than without AI (3732 of 5760 readings, 64.8%). The specificity per patient with AI aid (5504 of 5760 readings, 95.6%) was noninferior to that without AI aid (5217 of 5760 readings, 90.6%), with a difference of +5.0% (95% CI: +2.0, +8.0; P = .001 for noninferiority). AI shortened the average reading time by 6.3 seconds per examination (95% CI: -12.5, -0.1; P = .046). The sensitivity by patient gain was significant in all regions (+8.0% to +16.2%; P < .05) but shoulder and clavicle and spine (+4.2% and +2.6%; P = .12 and .52).

topic: AI aid for appendicular skeletal fracture detection by emergency physicians and radiologists
authors: Duron L, Ducarouge A, Gillibert A, et al.
title: Assessment of an AI Aid in Detection of Adult Appendicular Skeletal Fractures by Emergency Physicians and Radiologists: A Multicenter Cross-sectional Diagnostic Study
key_points: 600 adult trauma patients from 17 French centres were retrospectively included; 6 radiologists and 6 emergency physicians read radiographs with and without AI bounding-box aid. Several co-authors were affiliated with Gleamer, the developer of the AI software evaluated (vendor-affiliated study).
The AI aid improved reader sensitivity by 8.7% (95% CI: 3.1, 14.2) and specificity by 4.1% (95% CI: 0.5, 7.7).
False-positive fractures per patient fell by 41.9% (95% CI: 12.8, 61.3) in patients without fractures; mean reading time fell by 15.0% (not statistically significant, P = .12).
Stand-alone AI (newer release) had an AUC of 0.94 (95% CI: 0.92, 0.96), greater than all unaided readers.
key_points_pt: Foram incluídos retrospetivamente 600 doentes adultos com traumatismo de 17 centros franceses; 6 radiologistas e 6 médicos de urgência leram as radiografias com e sem marcação das fraturas por IA (caixas delimitadoras). Vários coautores estavam afiliados à Gleamer, a empresa que desenvolveu o software de IA avaliado (estudo com ligação ao fabricante).
O apoio de IA aumentou a sensibilidade dos leitores em 8,7% (IC 95%: 3,1–14,2) e a especificidade em 4,1% (IC 95%: 0,5–7,7).
O número de fraturas falso-positivas por doente diminuiu 41,9% (IC 95%: 12,8–61,3) nos doentes sem fratura; o tempo médio de leitura diminuiu 15,0% (sem significado estatístico, P = 0,12).
A IA isolada (versão mais recente) obteve uma AUC de 0,94 (IC 95%: 0,92–0,96), superior à de todos os leitores sem apoio.
abstract_excerpt: Between 2016 and 2018, 600 adult patients in whom multiview radiographs had been obtained after a recent trauma, with or without one or more fractures of shoulder, arm, hand, pelvis, leg, and foot, were retrospectively included from 17 French medical centers. [...] Six radiologists and six emergency physicians were asked to detect and localize fractures with (n = 300) and fractures without (n = 300) the aid of software highlighting boxes around AI-detected fractures. [...] The AI aid improved the sensitivity of physicians by 8.7% (95% CI: 3.1, 14.2; P = .003 for superiority) and the specificity by 4.1% (95% CI: 0.5, 7.7; P < .001 for noninferiority) and reduced the average number of false-positive fractures per patient by 41.9% (95% CI: 12.8, 61.3; P = .02) in patients without fractures and the mean reading time by 15.0% (95% CI: -30.4, 3.8; P = .12). Finally, stand-alone performance of a newer release of the AI system was greater than that of all unaided readers, including skeletal expert radiologists, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.94 (95% CI: 0.92, 0.96).

topic: Clinically suspected (occult) scaphoid fracture with negative radiographs: CT vs MRI vs bone scintigraphy
authors: Mallee WH, Wang J, Poolman RW, et al.
title: Computed tomography versus magnetic resonance imaging versus bone scintigraphy for clinically suspected scaphoid fractures in patients with negative plain radiographs
key_points: Cochrane review of 11 studies of clinically suspected scaphoid fractures with normal initial radiographs (CT: 4 studies; MRI: 5; bone scintigraphy: 6; some studies assessed two tests).

Summary sensitivity/specificity: CT 0.72 (95% CI 0.36 to 0.92) / 0.99 (95% CI 0.71 to 1.00); MRI 0.88 (95% CI 0.64 to 0.97) / 1.00 (95% CI 0.38 to 1.00); bone scintigraphy 0.99 (95% CI 0.69 to 1.00) / 0.86 (95% CI 0.73 to 0.94).

Indirect comparisons suggested significantly higher accuracy for bone scintigraphy than for CT and MRI (CT and MRI comparable); but with a low median prevalence of true fracture (20%), the lower specificity of bone scintigraphy is problematic, and the number of over-treated patients is substantially lower with CT and MRI.

Confidence intervals were wide for all three tests (only 11 studies, results mostly from indirect comparisons); bone scintigraphy is also more invasive, involves radiation exposure and delays diagnosis by at least 72 hours.
key_points_pt: Revisão Cochrane de 11 estudos de suspeita clínica de fratura do escafoide com radiografias iniciais normais (TC: 4 estudos; RM: 5; cintigrafia óssea: 6; alguns estudos avaliaram dois exames).

As comparações indiretas sugeriram exatidão significativamente superior da cintigrafia óssea face à TC e à RM (TC e RM comparáveis); contudo, com uma prevalência mediana baixa de fratura verdadeira (20%), a menor especificidade da cintigrafia é problemática e o número de doentes sobretratados é substancialmente menor com TC e RM.

Os intervalos de confiança foram amplos para os três exames (apenas 11 estudos, resultados maioritariamente de comparações indiretas); a cintigrafia óssea é também mais invasiva, implica exposição a radiação e atrasa o diagnóstico pelo menos 72 horas.
abstract_excerpt: We included 11 studies that looked at diagnostic accuracy of one or two index tests: four studies (277 suspected fractures) looked at CT, five studies (221 suspected fractures) looked at MRI and six studies (543 suspected fractures) looked at BS. [...] As few studies made direct comparisons between tests with the same participants, our results are based on data from indirect comparisons, which means that these results are more susceptible to bias due to confounding. [...] Summary sensitivity and specificity of CT were 0.72 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.36 to 0.92) and 0.99 (95% CI 0.71 to 1.00); for MRI, these were 0.88 (95% CI 0.64 to 0.97) and 1.00 (95% CI 0.38 to 1.00); for BS, these were 0.99 (95% CI 0.69 to 1.00) and 0.86 (95% CI 0.73 to 0.94). Indirect comparisons suggest that diagnostic accuracy of BS was significantly higher than CT and MRI; and CT and MRI have comparable diagnostic accuracy. The low prevalence of a true fracture among suspected fractures (median = 20%) means the lower specificity for BS is problematic. [...] Although quality of the included studies is moderate to good, findings are based on only 11 studies and the confidence intervals for the summary estimates are wide for all three tests. [...] However, physicians must keep in mind that BS is more invasive than the other modalities, with safety issues due to level of radiation exposure, as well as diagnostic delay of at least 72 hours. The number of overtreated patients is substantially lower with CT and MRI.

topic: Suspected scaphoid fracture: accuracy of follow-up radiographs, MRI, CT and bone scintigraphy (latent class analysis)
authors: Yin ZG, Zhang JB, Kan SL, Wang XG
title: Diagnostic accuracy of imaging modalities for suspected scaphoid fractures: meta-analysis combined with latent class analysis
journal: Journal of Bone and Joint Surgery. British Volume
key_points: Meta-analysis of 30 clinical studies combined with latent class analysis to account for the lack of a reference standard for suspected scaphoid fractures.
Estimated sensitivity/specificity: follow-up radiographs 91.1%/99.8%; bone scintigraphy 97.8%/93.5%; MRI 97.7%/99.8%; CT 85.2%/99.5%.
MRI was the most accurate test; follow-up radiographs and CT may be less sensitive, and bone scintigraphy less specific.
There was large between-study heterogeneity and imprecision for the sensitivity estimates of follow-up radiographs and CT.
key_points_pt: Meta-análise de 30 estudos clínicos combinada com análise de classes latentes, para contornar a ausência de padrão de referência na suspeita de fratura do escafoide.
Sensibilidade/especificidade estimadas: radiografias de controlo 91,1%/99,8%; cintigrafia óssea 97,8%/93,5%; RM 97,7%/99,8%; TC 85,2%/99,5%.
A RM foi o exame mais exato; as radiografias de controlo e a TC podem ser menos sensíveis e a cintigrafia óssea menos específica.
Houve grande heterogeneidade entre estudos e imprecisão nas estimativas de sensibilidade das radiografias de controlo e da TC.
abstract_excerpt: We performed a meta-analysis of 30 clinical studies on the diagnosis of suspected scaphoid fractures, in which agreement data between any of follow-up radiographs, bone scintigraphy, magnetic resonance (MR) imaging, or CT could be obtained, and combined this with latent class analysis to infer the accuracy of these tests on the diagnosis of suspected scaphoid fractures in the absence of an established standard. The estimated sensitivity and specificity were respectively 91.1% and 99.8% for follow-up radiographs, 97.8% and 93.5% for bone scintigraphy, 97.7% and 99.8% for MRI, and 85.2% and 99.5% for CT. The results were generally robust in multiple sensitivity analyses. There was large between-study heterogeneity for the sensitivity of follow-up radiographs and CT, and imprecision about their sensitivity estimates. If we acknowledge the lack of a reference standard for diagnosing suspected scaphoid fractures, MRI is the most accurate test; follow-up radiographs and CT may be less sensitive, and bone scintigraphy less specific.

topic: Distal radius fracture: radiographic thresholds in the 2010 AAOS clinical practice guideline (superseded by the 2020 AAOS/ASSH guideline, summary PMID 35143462)
authors: Lichtman DM, Bindra RR, Boyer MI, et al.
title: Treatment of distal radius fractures
journal: Journal of the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons
key_points: AAOS clinical practice guideline based on a systematic review: of 29 recommendations, none was graded strong, most were inconclusive or consensus, seven were weak and five were moderate-strength.

Moderate-strength recommendation: surgical fixation rather than cast fixation for fractures with post-reduction radial shortening >3 mm, dorsal tilt >10 degrees, or intra-articular displacement or step-off >2 mm.
Moderate-strength recommendation: obtain a post-reduction true lateral radiograph of the carpus to assess radioulnar joint alignment.
key_points_pt: Norma de orientação clínica da AAOS baseada em revisão sistemática: das 29 recomendações, nenhuma foi de grau forte, a maioria foi inconclusiva ou de consenso, sete foram fracas e cinco de força moderada.

Recomendação de força moderada: fixação cirúrgica em vez de imobilização gessada nas fraturas com encurtamento radial pós-redução >3 mm, inclinação dorsal >10 graus ou desvio/degrau intra-articular >2 mm.
Recomendação de força moderada: realizar radiografia de perfil verdadeiro do carpo após redução para avaliar o alinhamento da articulação radiocubital.
abstract_excerpt: The clinical practice guideline is based on a systematic review of published studies on the treatment of distal radius fractures in adults. None of the 29 recommendations made by the work group was graded as strong; most are graded as inconclusive or consensus; seven are graded as weak. The remaining five moderate-strength recommendations include surgical fixation, rather than cast fixation, for fractures with postreduction radial shortening >3 mm, dorsal tilt >10 degrees , or intra-articular displacement or step-off >2 mm; use of rigid immobilization rather than removable splints for nonsurgical treatment; making a postreduction true lateral radiograph of the carpus to assess dorsal radial ulnar joint alignment; [...]

topic: Garden classification of femoral neck fractures: inter- and intraobserver reliability
authors: Masionis P, Uvarovas V, Mazarevičius G, et al.
title: The reliability of a Garden, AO and simple II stage classifications for intracapsular hip fractures
key_points: Six observers classified 136 blinded AP and lateral radiographs of femoral neck fractures twice, one month apart, using the four-stage Garden, AO and a simple two-stage classification.
Overall agreement was fair for AO (0.22) and Garden (0.33); the simple two-stage classification performed best (0.35 to 0.83; multi-rater agreement 0.50, moderate).

The authors concluded that the four-stage Garden and AO classifications should be avoided in clinical use because of poor reproducibility, and only the simple two-stage classification showed sufficient reliability; observer experience did not change agreement.
key_points_pt: Seis observadores classificaram duas vezes, com um mês de intervalo, 136 radiografias (incidências AP e perfil) de fraturas do colo do fémur, avaliadas em ocultação, usando as classificações de Garden (4 estádios), AO e uma classificação simples em 2 estádios.

A concordância global foi razoável para a AO (0,22) e para Garden (0,33); a classificação simples em 2 estádios teve o melhor desempenho (0,35 a 0,83; concordância entre múltiplos avaliadores 0,50, moderada).

Os autores concluíram que as classificações de Garden em 4 estádios e AO devem ser evitadas na prática clínica pela fraca reprodutibilidade, e que apenas a classificação simples em 2 estádios mostrou fiabilidade suficiente; a experiência dos observadores não alterou a concordância.
abstract_excerpt: Four orthopaedic trauma surgeons (two of them professors) and two senior orthopaedic trauma residents were invited to evaluated 136 blinded anterior-posterior and lateral X-rays of patients with femoral neck fractures. Observers classified fractures according to IV stage Garden, AO and simple II stage classifications. The exercise was repeated after one month on same but randomised X-rays. [...] RESULTS: AO classification showed an overall agreement of 0.22 (fair agreement). Garden classification had overall reliability slightly higher than AO, but matching same fair agreement group (0.33). II stage classification provided the highest estimates: from 0.35 (fair agreement) to 0.83 (almost perfect agreement) and multi-rater agreement of 0.50 (moderate agreement). There was seen no difference in intra- and interobserver agreement between observer groups (professors, trauma surgeons and trauma residents) [...] Despite this finding, IV stage Garden and AO classifications should be avoided in clinical use because of poor reproducibility. Only simple II stage classification showed sufficient intra- and interobserver reliability.

topic: Radiographically occult hip fracture in elderly patients: frequency and role of advanced imaging (MRI, CT, bone scan)
authors: Haj-Mirzaian A, Eng J, Khorasani R, et al.
title: Use of Advanced Imaging for Radiographically Occult Hip Fracture in Elderly Patients: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
key_points: 35 studies (2992 patients; mean age 76.8 years) of elderly patients with clinically suspected hip fracture but no radiographic evidence of a surgical hip fracture, using MRI as reference standard.

Radiographically occult surgical hip fracture frequency was 39% (95% CI: 35%, 43%) with no definite radiographic fracture and 92% (95% CI: 83%, 98%) with an isolated greater trochanter fracture on radiographs.
Occult fracture was more frequent in patients aged at least 80 years (44%), with an equivocal radiographic report (58%) and with a history of trauma (41%).

CT and bone scanning had comparable performance (P = .67), with sensitivities of 79% and 87% respectively (low strength of evidence); advanced imaging, preferably MRI, may be clinically appropriate in all such patients.
key_points_pt: 35 estudos (2992 doentes; idade média 76,8 anos) de idosos com suspeita clínica de fratura da anca sem evidência radiográfica de fratura cirúrgica, com a RM como padrão de referência.

A frequência de fratura cirúrgica da anca radiograficamente oculta foi de 39% (IC 95%: 35–43%) sem fratura radiográfica definida e de 92% (IC 95%: 83–98%) quando a radiografia mostrava fratura isolada do grande trocânter.
A fratura oculta foi mais frequente em doentes com idade igual ou superior a 80 anos (44%), com relatório radiográfico duvidoso (58%) e com antecedentes de traumatismo (41%).

A TC e a cintigrafia óssea tiveram desempenho comparável (P = 0,67), com sensibilidades de 79% e 87%, respetivamente (baixa força de evidência); a imagiologia avançada, preferencialmente RM, pode ser clinicamente apropriada em todos estes doentes.
abstract_excerpt: Results Thirty-five studies were identified (2992 patients; mean age, 76.8 years ± 6.0 [standard deviation]; 66% female). The frequency of radiographically occult surgical hip fracture was 39% (1110 of 2835 patients; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 35%, 43%) in studies of patients with no definite radiographic fracture and 92% (134 of 157 patients; 95% CI: 83%, 98%) in studies of patients with radiographic evidence of isolated GT fracture (moderate SOE). The frequency of occult fracture was higher in patients aged at least 80 years (44%, 529 of 1184), those with an equivocal radiographic report (58%, 71 of 126), and those with a history of trauma (41%, 977 of 2370) (moderate SOE). CT and bone scanning yielded comparable diagnostic performance in the detection of radiographically occult hip fracture (P = .67), with a sensitivity of 79% and 87%, respectively (low SOE). Conclusion Elderly patients with acute hip pain and negative or equivocal findings at initial radiography have a high frequency of occult hip fractures. Therefore, the performance of advanced imaging (preferably MRI) may be clinically appropriate in all such patients.

topic: CT for occult proximal femoral fracture
authors: Kellock TT, Khurana B, Mandell JC
title: Diagnostic Performance of CT for Occult Proximal Femoral Fractures: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
key_points: 13 heterogeneously reported studies including 1248 patients (496 with hip fracture), with MRI or clinical follow-up as reference standard; there were 50 false-negative CT examinations.
Summary estimates for CT: sensitivity 94% and specificity 100%.
CT is a reasonable choice when MRI is contraindicated or unavailable, but MRI should be performed if clinical concern for hip fracture persists despite a normal CT.
key_points_pt: 13 estudos com relato heterogéneo, incluindo 1248 doentes (496 com fratura da anca), com RM ou seguimento clínico como padrão de referência; registaram-se 50 TC falso-negativas.
Estimativas agregadas para a TC: sensibilidade de 94% e especificidade de 100%.
A TC é uma opção razoável quando a RM está contraindicada ou indisponível, mas deve realizar-se RM se a suspeita clínica de fratura da anca persistir apesar de TC normal.
abstract_excerpt: Thirteen heterogeneously reported studies were assessed that included 1248 patients (496 with a hip fracture and 752 without) with MRI or clinical follow-up as the reference standard. There were 50 false-negative examinations. The summary estimate of sensitivity was 94% and of specificity was 100%. CONCLUSION. CT can be considered a reasonable choice when occult proximal femoral fracture is suspected clinically in patients for whom MRI is contraindicated or not readily available. However, for patients with ongoing clinical concern about hip fracture despite normal CT findings, MRI should be performed.

topic: Ottawa ankle rules for excluding ankle and mid-foot fractures
authors: Bachmann LM, Kolb E, Koller MT, Steurer J, ter Riet G
title: Accuracy of Ottawa ankle rules to exclude fractures of the ankle and mid-foot: systematic review
key_points: 32 studies met inclusion criteria; 27 studies reporting on 15 581 patients were meta-analysed.
Pooled negative likelihood ratios: ankle 0.08 (95% CI 0.03 to 0.18), mid-foot 0.08 (0.03 to 0.20), children (both regions) 0.07 (0.03 to 0.18).
At a 15% fracture prevalence, a negative rule gives a less than 1.4% probability of fracture.
Sensitivity of almost 100% with modest specificity; use should reduce unnecessary radiographs by 30-40%.
key_points_pt: 32 estudos cumpriram os critérios de inclusão; 27 estudos com 15 581 doentes foram incluídos na meta-análise.
Razões de verosimilhança negativas agregadas: tornozelo 0,08 (IC 95% 0,03–0,18), mediopé 0,08 (0,03–0,20), crianças (ambas as regiões) 0,07 (0,03–0,18).
Para uma prevalência de fratura de 15%, uma regra negativa implica uma probabilidade de fratura inferior a 1,4%.
Sensibilidade de quase 100% com especificidade modesta; a sua aplicação deverá reduzir as radiografias desnecessárias em 30–40%.
keywords: regras de Ottawa para o tornozelo
abstract_excerpt: RESULTS: 32 studies met the inclusion criteria and 27 studies reporting on 15 581 patients were used for meta-analysis. The pooled negative likelihood ratios for the ankle and mid-foot were 0.08 (95% confidence interval 0.03 to 0.18) and 0.08 (0.03 to 0.20), respectively. The pooled negative likelihood ratio for both regions in children was 0.07 (0.03 to 0.18). Applying these ratios to a 15% prevalence of fracture gave a less than 1.4% probability of actual fracture in these subgroups. CONCLUSIONS: Evidence supports the Ottawa ankle rules as an accurate instrument for excluding fractures of the ankle and mid-foot. The instrument has a sensitivity of almost 100% and a modest specificity, and its use should reduce the number of unnecessary radiographs by 30-40%.

topic: Danis-Weber classification of ankle fractures: reliability on radiographs
authors: Malek IA, Machani B, Mevcha AM, Hyder NH
title: Inter-observer reliability and intra-observer reproducibility of the Weber classification of ankle fractures
journal: Journal of Bone and Joint Surgery. British Volume
key_points: Five observers with varying experience classified 50 sets of blinded AP and lateral ankle radiographs twice, four weeks apart.
Inter-observer agreement: mean kappa 0.61 (0.59 to 0.63), proportion of agreement 78%.
Intra-observer agreement: mean kappa 0.74 (0.39 to 0.86), observed agreement 85%.
The Weber classification based on two radiographic views showed substantial inter-observer reliability and intra-observer reproducibility.
key_points_pt: Cinco observadores com experiência variável classificaram duas vezes, com quatro semanas de intervalo, 50 conjuntos de radiografias do tornozelo (AP e perfil), avaliados em ocultação.
Concordância interobservador: kappa médio de 0,61 (0,59–0,63), proporção de concordância de 78%.
Concordância intraobservador: kappa médio de 0,74 (0,39–0,86), concordância observada de 85%.
A classificação de Weber baseada em duas incidências radiográficas mostrou fiabilidade interobservador e reprodutibilidade intraobservador substanciais.
abstract_excerpt: Five observers with varying clinical experience reviewed 50 sets of blinded radiographs. The same observers reviewed the same radiographs again after an interval of four weeks. [...] For inter-observer agreement, the mean kappa value was 0.61 (0.59 to 0.63) and the proportion of agreement was 78% (76% to 79%) and for intra-observer agreement the mean kappa value was 0.74 (0.39 to 0.86) with an 85% (60% to 93%) observed agreement. These results show that the Weber classification of fractures of the ankle based on two radiological views has substantial inter-observer reliability and intra-observer reproducibility.

topic: Pediatric physeal (growth plate) fractures: epidemiology and Salter-Harris type distribution
authors: Peterson HA, Madhok R, Benson JT, Ilstrup DM, Melton LJ 3rd
title: Physeal fractures: Part 1. Epidemiology in Olmsted County, Minnesota, 1979-1988
key_points: Population-based study: 850 children sustained 951 physeal fractures over 10 years; male:female ratio 2:1.
Overall age- and sex-adjusted incidence of physeal fractures was 279.2 per 100,000 person-years (95% CI, 261.4-296.9); incidence peaked at 11-12 years in girls and 14 years in boys.
The phalanges of the fingers were the most common site (37% of physeal fractures).
Salter-Harris type II was the most common type (54%), but 149 fractures (16%) did not fit the Salter-Harris classification.
key_points_pt: Estudo de base populacional: 850 crianças sofreram 951 fraturas fisárias em 10 anos; razão sexo masculino:feminino de 2:1.
A incidência global ajustada à idade e ao sexo foi de 279,2 por 100 000 pessoas-ano (IC 95%: 261,4–296,9); a incidência foi máxima aos 11–12 anos nas raparigas e aos 14 anos nos rapazes.
As falanges dos dedos da mão foram a localização mais frequente (37% das fraturas fisárias).
O tipo II de Salter-Harris foi o mais frequente (54%), mas 149 fraturas (16%) não se enquadravam na classificação de Salter-Harris.
abstract_excerpt: Eight-hundred fifty children sustained 951 physeal fractures; 561 boys (66%) sustained 637 fractures, and 289 girls (34%) experienced 314 fractures. The male:female ratio was 2:1 and incidence rates were greatest among 11-12 year-old girls and 14-year-old boys. The overall age- and sex-adjusted incidence of physeal fractures was 279.2 per 100,000 person-years (95% confidence interval, 261.4-296.9). The most common site was the phalanges of fingers, which accounted for 37% of all physeal fractures. Salter-Harris type II was the most common type of fracture (54%), but 149 fractures (16%) did not fit into this classification.

topic: Anterior shoulder dislocation: prevalence of Hill-Sachs and Bankart lesions (first-time vs recurrent)
authors: Rutgers C, Verweij LPE, Priester-Vink S, et al.
title: Recurrence in traumatic anterior shoulder dislocations increases the prevalence of Hill-Sachs and Bankart lesions: a systematic review and meta-analysis
key_points: 22 studies (1920 shoulders) assessed after traumatic anterior dislocation by arthroscopy, MRI/MR arthrography or CT.
Hill-Sachs and Bankart lesions were more frequent after recurrent dislocations (85%; 66%) than after first-time dislocations (71%; 59%) (P < 0.01; P = 0.05).
Hill-Sachs lesions were more frequent after complete dislocations (82%) than after subluxations (54%; P < 0.01).
No significant difference between first-time and recurrent dislocations for bony Bankart, SLAP, rotator cuff tears, HAGL and ALPSA lesions; heterogeneity was substantial.
key_points_pt: 22 estudos (1920 ombros) avaliados após luxação anterior traumática por artroscopia, RM/artro-RM ou TC.
As lesões de Hill-Sachs e de Bankart foram mais frequentes após luxações recidivantes (85%; 66%) do que após primeiras luxações (71%; 59%) (P < 0,01; P = 0,05).
As lesões de Hill-Sachs foram mais frequentes após luxações completas (82%) do que após subluxações (54%; P < 0,01).
Sem diferença significativa entre primeira luxação e luxação recidivante para lesões de Bankart ósseo, SLAP, roturas da coifa dos rotadores, HAGL e ALPSA; a heterogeneidade foi substancial.
abstract_excerpt: Studies examining shoulders after traumatic anterior dislocations during arthroscopy or with MRI/MRA or CT published after 1999 were included. A total of 22 studies (1920 shoulders) were included. RESULTS: The proportion of Hill-Sachs and Bankart lesions was higher in recurrent dislocations (85%; 66%) compared to first-time dislocations (71%; 59%) and this was statistically significant (P < 0.01; P = 0.05). No significant difference between recurrent and first-time dislocations was observed for SLAP lesions, rotator-cuff tears, bony Bankart lesions, HAGL lesions and ALPSA lesions. The proportion of Hill-Sachs lesions was significantly higher in complete dislocations (82%) compared to subluxations (54%; P < 0.01). [...] However, results should be interpreted with caution due to substantial heterogeneity and large variance.

topic: Imaging modalities for diagnosis and quantification of Hill-Sachs lesions
authors: Vopat ML, Peebles LA, McBride T, et al.
title: Accuracy and Reliability of Imaging Modalities for the Diagnosis and Quantification of Hill-Sachs Lesions: A Systematic Review
key_points: Systematic review of 40 studies (2560 shoulders) on imaging of Hill-Sachs lesions in anterior shoulder instability.
For detecting Hill-Sachs lesions, CT arthrography had the highest reported accuracy (median 91%; range 66%-100%) and sensitivity (median 94%; range 50%-100%).

For quantification, intraobserver reliability was highest for 3D CT (ICC 0.916-0.999), followed by 2D CT (ICC 0.858-0.861) and MRI (ICC 0.28-0.97); interobserver reliability: 3D CT ICC 0.772-0.996, 2D CT ICC 0.721-0.879, MRI kappa 0.444-0.700.
key_points_pt: Revisão sistemática de 40 estudos (2560 ombros) sobre imagiologia das lesões de Hill-Sachs na instabilidade anterior do ombro.
Na deteção das lesões de Hill-Sachs, a artro-TC teve a maior exatidão relatada (mediana 91%; intervalo 66–100%) e a maior sensibilidade (mediana 94%; intervalo 50–100%).

Na quantificação, a fiabilidade intraobservador foi maior na TC 3D (ICC 0,916–0,999), seguida da TC 2D (ICC 0,858–0,861) e da RM (ICC 0,28–0,97); fiabilidade interobservador: TC 3D ICC 0,772–0,996, TC 2D ICC 0,721–0,879, RM kappa 0,444–0,700.
abstract_excerpt: RESULTS: Forty studies (2,560 shoulders) met the inclusion criteria and were assessed. For diagnosing the presence of Hill-Sachs lesions, computed tomography (CT) arthrography had the highest reported accuracy (median, 91%; range, 66%-100%). For the same assessment, CT arthrography also had the greatest reported sensitivity (median, 94%; range, 50%-100%). For the quantification of Hill-Sachs lesion parameters, reported intraobserver reliabilities were highest for 3-dimensional (3D) CT (intraclass correlation coefficient [ICC] range, 0.916-0.999), followed by 2-dimensional CT (ICC range, 0.858-0.861) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) (ICC range, 0.28-0.97). For the same quantification parameters, interobserver reliabilities were also reported for 3D CT (ICC range, 0.772-0.996), 2-dimensional CT (ICC range, 0.721-0.879), and MRI (κ range, 0.444-0.700).

topic: Genant semiquantitative (SQ) method for vertebral fracture assessment
authors: Genant HK, Wu CY, van Kuijk C, Nevitt MC
title: Vertebral fracture assessment using a semiquantitative technique
journal: Journal of Bone and Mineral Research
key_points: Describes and assesses the reliability of the semiquantitative visual approach for prevalent and incident vertebral fractures on conventional radiographs, compared with quantitative morphometry.
Applied by three independent observers to 57 postmenopausal women aged 65-75 years.
Showed excellent intraobserver and good interobserver agreement; can be applied reliably when performed with well-defined criteria.
key_points_pt: Descrição e avaliação da fiabilidade do método visual semiquantitativo para fraturas vertebrais prevalentes e incidentes em radiografia convencional, comparado com a morfometria quantitativa.
Aplicado por três observadores independentes a 57 mulheres pós-menopáusicas com 65–75 anos.
Mostrou concordância intraobservador excelente e interobservador boa; pode ser aplicado de forma fiável quando usado com critérios bem definidos.
abstract_excerpt: The inter- and intraobserver variability was determined for a semiquantitative visual approach that we routinely use in clinical studies for assessing prevalent and incident vertebral fractures. In addition, the semiquantitative approach was compared with a quantitative morpho-metric approach. The incidence and prevalence of vertebral fractures were determined in 57 postmenopausal women (age 65–75 years) by three independent observers. [...] The results show excellent intraobserver agreement and good interobserver agreement for the semiquantitative technique. We conclude that the semiquantitative approach can be applied reliably in vertebral fracture assessment when performed using well-defined criteria.

topic: Under-reporting of osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures on CT; value of sagittal reformations
authors: Williams AL, Al-Busaidi A, Sparrow PJ, Adams JE, Whitehouse RW
title: Under-reporting of osteoporotic vertebral fractures on computed tomography
key_points: Thoracic CT scans of 100 consecutive men and 100 consecutive women over 55 years (192 analysed; mean age 70.1 years) were reviewed for moderate (25-40% height loss) or severe (>40% height loss) vertebral fractures from T1 to L1 using an established semiquantitative method.
38 (19.8%) patients had one or more moderate to severe vertebral fractures, but only 5 (13%) were correctly reported in the official report.
Sensitivity of axial CT images for vertebral fracture was 0.35; sagittal reformations are strongly recommended to improve detection.
key_points_pt: Foram revistas TC torácicas de 100 homens e 100 mulheres consecutivos com mais de 55 anos (192 analisados; idade média 70,1 anos) para fraturas vertebrais moderadas (perda de altura de 25–40%) ou graves (perda de altura >40%) de T1 a L1, com um método semiquantitativo estabelecido.
38 doentes (19,8%) tinham uma ou mais fraturas vertebrais moderadas a graves, mas apenas 5 (13%) foram corretamente descritos no relatório oficial.
A sensibilidade das imagens axiais de TC para fratura vertebral foi de 0,35; recomendam-se fortemente reformatações sagitais para melhorar a deteção.
abstract_excerpt: The thoracic CT scans of 100 consecutive male and 100 consecutive female patients over 55 years were reviewed. [...] The presence of moderate (25-40% height loss) or severe (>40% height loss) vertebral fractures between T1 and L1 was determined using an established semi-quantitative method and confirmed by morphological measurement. [...] Scans of 192 patients were analysed (95 female; 97 male); mean age 70.1 years. Thirty-eight (19.8%) patients had one or more moderate to severe vertebral fractures. Only 5 (13%) were correctly reported as having osteoporotic fractures in the official report. The sensitivity of axial CT images to vertebral fracture was 0.35. CONCLUSION: Incidental osteoporotic vertebral fractures are under-reported on CT. The sensitivity of axial images in detecting these fractures is poor. Sagittal reformations are strongly recommended to improve the detection rate.

topic: NEXUS low-risk criteria for cervical spine imaging after blunt trauma
authors: Hoffman JR, Mower WR, Wolfson AB, Todd KH, Zucker MI
title: Validity of a set of clinical criteria to rule out injury to the cervical spine in patients with blunt trauma. National Emergency X-Radiography Utilization Study Group
key_points: Prospective observational study at 21 US centres of 34,069 blunt trauma patients who underwent cervical spine radiography.
Low risk required all five criteria: no midline cervical tenderness, no focal neurologic deficit, normal alertness, no intoxication, and no painful distracting injury.

The rule identified all but 8 of 818 patients with cervical spine injury: sensitivity 99.0% (95% CI 98.0 to 99.6), NPV 99.8% (95% CI 99.6 to 100), specificity 12.9%; for clinically significant injury sensitivity was 99.6% (95% CI 98.6 to 100).
Imaging could have been avoided in 4309 (12.6%) of the 34,069 patients.
key_points_pt: Estudo observacional prospetivo em 21 centros dos EUA com 34 069 doentes com traumatismo fechado submetidos a radiografia da coluna cervical.

O baixo risco exigia os cinco critérios: ausência de dor à palpação da linha média cervical, ausência de défice neurológico focal, estado de alerta normal, ausência de intoxicação e ausência de lesão dolorosa distrativa.

A regra identificou todos exceto 8 dos 818 doentes com lesão da coluna cervical: sensibilidade 99,0% (IC 95% 98,0–99,6), valor preditivo negativo 99,8% (IC 95% 99,6–100), especificidade 12,9%; para lesão clinicamente significativa a sensibilidade foi de 99,6% (IC 95% 98,6–100).
A imagiologia poderia ter sido evitada em 4309 (12,6%) dos 34 069 doentes.
abstract_excerpt: We conducted a prospective, observational study of such a decision instrument at 21 centers across the United States. The decision instrument required patients to meet five criteria in order to be classified as having a low probability of injury: no midline cervical tenderness, no focal neurologic deficit, normal alertness, no intoxication, and no painful, distracting injury. We examined the performance of the decision rule in 34,069 patients who underwent radiography of the cervical spine after blunt trauma. RESULTS: The decision instrument identified all but 8 of the 818 patients who had cervical-spine injury (sensitivity, 99.0 percent [95 percent confidence interval, 98.0 to 99.6 percent]). The negative predictive value was 99.8 percent (95 percent confidence interval, 99.6 to 100 percent), the specificity was 12.9 percent, and the positive predictive value was 2.7 percent. [...] According to the results of assessment with the decision instrument, radiographic imaging could have been avoided in the cases of 4309 (12.6 percent) of the 34,069 evaluated patients.

topic: Canadian C-spine rule: derivation
authors: Stiell IG, Wells GA, Vandemheen KL, et al.
title: The Canadian C-spine rule for radiography in alert and stable trauma patients
key_points: Prospective derivation cohort (convenience sample) of 8924 alert (GCS 15), stable adults with blunt head/neck trauma in 10 Canadian EDs; 151 (1.7%) had clinically important C-spine injury.

The rule asks three questions: any high-risk factor mandating radiography (age >=65 years, dangerous mechanism, or paresthesias in extremities); any low-risk factor allowing safe assessment of range of motion; and whether the patient can actively rotate the neck 45 degrees left and right.

By cross-validation in the derivation cohort: sensitivity 100% (95% CI, 98%-100%) and specificity 42.5% (95% CI, 40%-44%) for clinically important injury; potential radiography ordering rate 58.2%. Prospective validation in other cohorts was still required.
key_points_pt: Coorte prospetiva de derivação (amostra de conveniência) com 8924 adultos alerta (GCS 15) e estáveis com traumatismo fechado da cabeça/pescoço em 10 serviços de urgência canadianos; 151 (1,7%) tinham lesão cervical clinicamente importante.

A regra tem três perguntas: existe algum fator de alto risco que obrigue a radiografia (idade >=65 anos, mecanismo perigoso ou parestesias nas extremidades); existe algum fator de baixo risco que permita avaliar com segurança a mobilidade; e o doente consegue rodar ativamente o pescoço 45 graus para a esquerda e para a direita.

Por validação cruzada na coorte de derivação: sensibilidade de 100% (IC 95%: 98–100%) e especificidade de 42,5% (IC 95%: 40–44%) para lesão clinicamente importante; taxa potencial de pedido de radiografia de 58,2%. Era ainda necessária validação prospetiva noutras coortes.
abstract_excerpt: SETTING: Ten EDs in large Canadian community and university hospitals. PATIENTS: Convenience sample of 8924 adults (mean age, 37 years) who presented to the ED with blunt trauma to the head/neck, stable vital signs, and a Glasgow Coma Scale score of 15. [...] Among the study sample, 151 (1.7%) had important C-spine injury. The resultant model and final Canadian C-Spine Rule comprises 3 main questions: (1) is there any high-risk factor present that mandates radiography (ie, age >/=65 years, dangerous mechanism, or paresthesias in extremities)? (2) is there any low-risk factor present that allows safe assessment of range of motion (ie, simple rear-end motor vehicle collision, sitting position in ED, ambulatory at any time since injury, delayed onset of neck pain, or absence of midline C-spine tenderness)? and (3) is the patient able to actively rotate neck 45 degrees to the left and right? By cross-validation, this rule had 100% sensitivity (95% confidence interval [CI], 98%-100%) and 42.5% specificity (95% CI, 40%-44%) for identifying 151 clinically important C-spine injuries. The potential radiography ordering rate would be 58.2%. [...] If prospectively validated in other cohorts, this rule has the potential to significantly reduce practice variation and inefficiency in ED use of C-spine radiography.

topic: Canadian C-spine rule versus NEXUS low-risk criteria: head-to-head comparison
authors: Stiell IG, Clement CM, McKnight RD, et al.
title: The Canadian C-spine rule versus the NEXUS low-risk criteria in patients with trauma
key_points: Prospective cohort in nine Canadian EDs: 8283 alert, stable trauma patients, 169 (2.0%) with clinically important cervical spine injury.
Excluding indeterminate cases, the CCR was more sensitive (99.4% vs 90.7%) and more specific (45.1% vs 36.8%) than the NEXUS low-risk criteria (P<0.001).
CCR use would have resulted in lower radiography rates (55.9% vs 66.6%); the CCR would have missed 1 patient and NEXUS 16 patients with important injuries.
In 845 (10.2%) patients physicians did not evaluate range of motion as required by the CCR.
key_points_pt: Coorte prospetiva em nove serviços de urgência canadianos: 8283 doentes alerta e estáveis com traumatismo, 169 (2,0%) com lesão cervical clinicamente importante.
Excluindo os casos indeterminados, a regra canadiana foi mais sensível (99,4% vs 90,7%) e mais específica (45,1% vs 36,8%) do que os critérios de baixo risco NEXUS (P<0,001).
A regra canadiana resultaria em menos radiografias (55,9% vs 66,6%); teria falhado 1 doente e os critérios NEXUS 16 doentes com lesões importantes.
Em 845 doentes (10,2%) os médicos não avaliaram a mobilidade cervical, como exige a regra canadiana.
abstract_excerpt: We conducted a prospective cohort study in nine Canadian emergency departments comparing the CCR and NLC as applied to alert patients with trauma who were in stable condition. [...] RESULTS: Among the 8283 patients, 169 (2.0 percent) had clinically important cervical-spine injuries. In 845 (10.2 percent) of the patients, physicians did not evaluate range of motion as required by the CCR algorithm. In analyses that excluded these indeterminate cases, the CCR was more sensitive than the NLC (99.4 percent vs. 90.7 percent, P<0.001) and more specific (45.1 percent vs. 36.8 percent, P<0.001) for injury, and its use would have resulted in lower radiography rates (55.9 percent vs. 66.6 percent, P<0.001). [...] The CCR would have missed 1 patient and the NLC would have missed 16 patients with important injuries.

topic: CT versus radiography for cervical spine injury screening
title: Computed tomography versus plain radiography to screen for cervical spine injury: a meta-analysis
key_points: Meta-analysis of seven studies (of 712 articles screened; literature from January 1995 to June 2004) reporting both plain radiography and CT for blunt cervical spine injury; no randomized trials.
Pooled sensitivity for identifying patients with cervical spine injury: radiography 52% (95% CI 47, 56%) vs CT 98% (95% CI 96, 99%); combined specificity could not be calculated.

CT should be the initial screening test in patients at very high risk (e.g. significantly depressed mental status); evidence was insufficient to replace radiography with CT in low-risk patients who still require imaging.
key_points_pt: Meta-análise de sete estudos (de 712 artigos avaliados; literatura de janeiro de 1995 a junho de 2004) com radiografia e TC na lesão da coluna cervical por traumatismo fechado; sem ensaios aleatorizados.
Sensibilidade agregada para identificar doentes com lesão cervical: radiografia 52% (IC 95% 47–56%) vs TC 98% (IC 95% 96–99%); não foi possível calcular a especificidade combinada.

A TC deve ser o exame de rastreio inicial nos doentes de risco muito elevado (p. ex., alteração significativa do estado de consciência); a evidência foi insuficiente para substituir a radiografia pela TC em doentes de baixo risco que ainda necessitem de imagem.
abstract_excerpt: We conducted a MEDLINE search for articles published from January 1995 through June 2004, manually reviewed bibliographies, and hand searched four journals. Studies were included if they contained data on the performance of both plain radiography and CT in the detection of patients with blunt cervical spine injuries. Both authors screened titles and abstracts identified by the search and seven of the 712 articles met all inclusion criteria. [...] RESULTS: Patient entry criteria were highly variable for each study and there were no randomized controlled trials. For identifying patients with cervical spine injury, the pooled sensitivity for cervical spine plain radiography was 52% (95% CI 47, 56%) and for CT was 98% (95% CI 96, 99%). [...] Due to limitations of the gold standard tests in each study, a calculation of a combined specificity was not possible. CONCLUSION: Despite the absence of a randomized controlled trial, ample evidence exists that CT significantly outperforms plain radiography as a screening test for patients at very high risk of cervical spine injury and thus CT should be the initial screening test in those patients with a significantly depressed mental status. There is insufficient evidence to suggest that cervical spine CT should replace plain radiography as the initial screening test for less injured patients who are at low risk for cervical spine injury but still require a screening radiographic examination.

topic: ACR Appropriateness Criteria: acute spinal trauma (imaging selection)
authors: Expert Panel on Neurological Imaging; Hassankhani A, Freeman CW, Banks J, et al.
title: ACR Appropriateness Criteria® Acute Spinal Trauma: 2024 Update
journal: Journal of the American College of Radiology
key_points: Evidence-based ACR guideline (2024 update, published 2025) on imaging of acute blunt spine trauma, using GRADE-adapted evidence review and the RAND/UCLA Appropriateness Method.
CT is generally the first-line imaging modality for acute blunt spine trauma because it is fast, accurate and easily accessible.
Overuse of imaging is associated with prolonged emergency visits and unnecessary admissions, whereas failure to identify injuries can have severe consequences.
key_points_pt: Norma de orientação do ACR baseada na evidência (atualização de 2024, publicada em 2025) sobre imagiologia do traumatismo vertebral fechado agudo, com revisão da evidência adaptada do GRADE e método RAND/UCLA.
A TC é geralmente a modalidade de imagem de primeira linha no traumatismo vertebral fechado agudo por ser rápida, exata e facilmente acessível.
O uso excessivo de imagiologia associa-se a permanências prolongadas na urgência e internamentos desnecessários, enquanto a falha na identificação de lesões pode ter consequências graves.
abstract_excerpt: Due to its wide spectrum of injury patterns, imaging of acute blunt spine trauma can present many challenges. CT is generally the first-line imaging modality, as it is fast, accurate, and easily accessible. Choice of appropriate imaging is important, as overuse of imaging is associated with prolonged emergency visits and unnecessary hospital admission, potentially leading to iatrogenic injuries and an increase in economic burden. In contrast, failure to identify injuries can have severe consequences. [...] Established methodology principles such as Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation or GRADE are adapted to evaluate the evidence. The RAND/UCLA Appropriateness Method User Manual provides the methodology to determine the appropriateness of imaging and treatment procedures for specific clinical scenarios.

topic: ACR Appropriateness Criteria: acute hip pain / suspected hip fracture
authors: Expert Panel on Musculoskeletal Imaging; Bartolotta RJ, Ha AS, Bateni CP, et al.
title: ACR Appropriateness Criteria® Acute Hip Pain: 2024 Update
journal: Journal of the American College of Radiology
key_points: Hip fractures cannot be reliably diagnosed or excluded by physical examination alone.
Radiographs are the initial imaging modality of choice for acute hip pain.
Specific scenarios in which cross-sectional imaging (CT and/or MRI) should also be obtained are addressed as separate variants.
key_points_pt: As fraturas da anca não podem ser diagnosticadas nem excluídas de forma fiável apenas pelo exame objetivo.
A radiografia é a modalidade de imagem inicial de eleição na dor aguda da anca.
Os cenários específicos em que se deve também obter imagem seccional (TC e/ou RM) são tratados como variantes separadas.
abstract_excerpt: Imaging plays a crucial role in the evaluation of these injuries, noting that hip fractures cannot be reliably diagnosed or excluded via physical examination alone. Radiographs are the initial imaging modality of choice for acute hip pain. Several recent studies have evaluated specific scenarios in which cross-sectional imaging (CT and/or MRI) should also be obtained-these scenarios will be reviewed as separate variants within this document.

topic: ACR Appropriateness Criteria: acute hand and wrist trauma
authors: Expert Panel on Musculoskeletal Imaging; Torabi M, Lenchik L, Beaman FD, et al.
title: ACR Appropriateness Criteria(®) Acute Hand and Wrist Trauma
journal: Journal of the American College of Radiology
key_points: In most hand and wrist injuries, conventional radiographs provide sufficient information to guide the treating clinician.
The guideline addresses seven common clinical variants and discusses appropriate use of CT, MRI, bone scan and ultrasound in addition to radiographs.
key_points_pt: Na maioria das lesões da mão e do punho, a radiografia convencional fornece informação suficiente para orientar o clínico assistente.
A norma aborda sete variantes clínicas frequentes e discute o uso apropriado de TC, RM, cintigrafia óssea e ecografia, para além da radiografia.
abstract_excerpt: Hand and wrist injuries are common reasons for musculoskeletal-related emergency department visits. Imaging is essential for evaluating many of these injuries. In most cases, conventional radiographs provide sufficient information to guide the treating clinician. This review focuses on seven common variants to guide diagnosis of hand and wrist injuries. In addition to radiographs, appropriate use of CT, MRI, bone scan, and ultrasound are discussed.

topic: ACR Appropriateness Criteria: acute trauma to the ankle (Ottawa rules variants)
authors: Expert Panel on Musculoskeletal Imaging; Smith SE, Chang EY, Ha AS, et al.
title: ACR Appropriateness Criteria® Acute Trauma to the Ankle
journal: Journal of the American College of Radiology
key_points: Defines best practices for imaging of patients presenting with acute ankle trauma.
Variants cover patients in whom the Ottawa rules can be evaluated, those with exclusionary criteria, those in whom the Ottawa rules cannot be evaluated, and specific injuries.
key_points_pt: Define as melhores práticas de imagiologia nos doentes com traumatismo agudo do tornozelo.
As variantes abrangem doentes em que as regras de Ottawa podem ser aplicadas, doentes com critérios de exclusão, doentes em que as regras de Ottawa não podem ser aplicadas e lesões específicas.
abstract_excerpt: This ACR Appropriateness Criteria defines best practices for imaging evaluation for several variants of patients presenting with acute ankle trauma. The variants include scenarios when Ottawa Rules can be evaluated, when there are exclusionary criteria, when Ottawa Rules cannot be evaluated, as well as specific injuries.

topic: Kellgren-Lawrence radiographic grading of osteoarthritis (original description)
title: Radiological assessment of osteo-arthrosis.
key_points: Original 1957 description of the radiographic grading of osteoarthrosis now known as the Kellgren-Lawrence (KL) classification: each radiograph is graded 0 to 4 with increasing severity (grade 0 = no OA, grade 4 = severe OA), with the grades described as 'none, doubtful, minimal, moderate, severe', as summarised by Kohn et al. 2016.
No abstract is available in PubMed (scanned article); per Kohn et al. 2016, the original authors (two observers) reported inter- and intraobserver correlation coefficients of 0.83 for the knee.
key_points_pt: Descrição original (1957) da graduação radiográfica da osteoartrose hoje conhecida como classificação de Kellgren-Lawrence (KL): cada radiografia é graduada de 0 a 4 por gravidade crescente (grau 0 = sem osteoartrose, grau 4 = osteoartrose grave), com os graus descritos como 'nenhuma, duvidosa, mínima, moderada, grave', conforme resumido por Kohn et al. 2016.

Sem resumo disponível na PubMed (artigo digitalizado); segundo Kohn et al. 2016, os autores originais (dois observadores) reportaram coeficientes de correlação inter e intraobservador de 0,83 para o joelho.
abstract_excerpt: No abstract in PubMed (scanned 1957 article, PMC1006995). Supporting text from Kohn et al. 2016 full text (PMC4925407): "Each radiograph was assigned a grade from 0 to 4, which they correlated to increasing severity of OA, with Grade 0 signifying no presence of OA and Grade 4 signifying severe OA"; "In their original paper, KL provided simple descriptions of each grade, 'none, doubtful, minimal, moderate, severe,' along with radiographic features considered evidence of OA"; "The authors report the inter- and intraobserver reliability correlation coefficient of the knee to both be 0.83".

topic: Kellgren-Lawrence classification: grade definitions, reliability and limitations
title: Classifications in Brief: Kellgren-Lawrence Classification of Osteoarthritis.
key_points: KL grade descriptors (Table 3): 0 = no joint space narrowing (JSN) or reactive changes; 1 = doubtful JSN, possible osteophytic lipping; 2 = definite osteophytes, possible JSN; 3 = moderate osteophytes, definite JSN, some sclerosis, possible bone-end deformity; 4 = large osteophytes, marked JSN, severe sclerosis, definite bone-end deformity.

Kellgren and Lawrence reported inter- and intraobserver correlation coefficients of 0.83 for the knee; Schiphof et al. found reproducibility depends on which grade description is used (weighted kappa 0.66, 0.69 and 0.63 for three alternative descriptions vs 0.41 for the original description and 0.35 for a fifth description).

Limitations: Kellgren and Lawrence never explicitly specified which radiographic features correspond to which grade, and the system has been criticised for assuming a linear radiographic progression of OA.
key_points_pt: Descritores dos graus KL (Tabela 3): 0 = sem redução da interlinha articular nem alterações reativas; 1 = redução duvidosa da interlinha, possível esboço osteofitário; 2 = osteófitos definidos, possível redução da interlinha; 3 = osteófitos moderados, redução definida da interlinha, alguma esclerose, possível deformidade das extremidades ósseas; 4 = osteófitos volumosos, redução marcada da interlinha, esclerose grave, deformidade definida das extremidades ósseas.

Kellgren e Lawrence reportaram coeficientes de correlação inter e intraobservador de 0,83 para o joelho; Schiphof et al. verificaram que a reprodutibilidade depende da descrição dos graus utilizada (kappa ponderado 0,66, 0,69 e 0,63 para três descrições alternativas vs 0,41 para a descrição original e 0,35 para uma quinta descrição).

Limitações: Kellgren e Lawrence nunca especificaram explicitamente que achados radiográficos correspondem a cada grau, e o sistema tem sido criticado por assumir uma progressão radiográfica linear da osteoartrose.
abstract_excerpt: No abstract in PubMed. Full text (PMC4925407): "Each radiograph was assigned a grade from 0 to 4, which they correlated to increasing severity of OA, with Grade 0 signifying no presence of OA and Grade 4 signifying severe OA"; Table 3, KL row: "0: No JSN or reactive changes" ... "2: Definite osteophytes, possible JSN" ... "4: Large osteophytes, marked JSN, severe sclerosis, definite bone ends deformity"; "The authors report the inter- and intraobserver reliability correlation coefficient of the knee to both be 0.83"; Schiphof et al.: "the reproducibility of three of the descriptions was 'good' (weighted κ = 0.66, 0.69, 0.63), whereas the reproducibility of the original description and a fifth description was 'moderate' and 'poor' (weighted κ = 0.41 and 0.35, respectively)"; "they never explicitly specified which radiographic features correspond to which grade".

topic: Diagnostic accuracy of knee MRI for ACL and meniscal tears (meta-analysis)
title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of the diagnostic accuracy of MRI for suspected ACL and meniscal tears of the knee.
key_points: Meta-analysis of prospective studies with arthroscopy as reference standard: MRI summary sensitivity 87% (95% CI 77-94%) and specificity 93% (95% CI 91-96%) for ACL tears (14 studies).
Medial meniscal tears: sensitivity 89% (95% CI 83-94%), specificity 88% (95% CI 82-93%); lateral meniscal tears: sensitivity 78% (95% CI 66-87%), specificity 95% (95% CI 91-97%) (19 studies each).
Magnetic field strength had no significant effect on accuracy; most studies had a high or unclear risk of bias, and too few ultrasound studies existed for meta-analysis.
key_points_pt: Meta-análise de estudos prospetivos com artroscopia como padrão de referência: sensibilidade agregada da ressonância magnética de 87% (IC 95% 77-94%) e especificidade de 93% (IC 95% 91-96%) para roturas do ligamento cruzado anterior (14 estudos).

Roturas do menisco medial: sensibilidade 89% (IC 95% 83-94%), especificidade 88% (IC 95% 82-93%); roturas do menisco lateral: sensibilidade 78% (IC 95% 66-87%), especificidade 95% (IC 95% 91-97%) (19 estudos cada).

A intensidade do campo magnético não teve efeito significativo na acuidade; a maioria dos estudos tinha risco de viés elevado ou incerto e os estudos de ecografia eram insuficientes para meta-análise.
