abstract_excerpt: The summary estimates of sensitivity and specificity of MRI were 87 % (95 % CI 77-94 %) and 93 % (95 % CI 91-96 %), respectively, for ACL tears; 89 % (95 % CI 83-94 %) and 88 % (95 % CI 82-93 %), respectively, for medial meniscal tears; and 78 % (95 % CI 66-87 %) and 95 % (95 % CI 91-97 %), respectively, for lateral meniscal tears. Magnetic field strength had no significant effect on accuracy. Most studies had a high or unclear risk of bias. There were an insufficient number of studies that evaluated US to perform a meta-analysis.

topic: Rotator cuff tear imaging accuracy: MRI vs MR arthrography vs ultrasound (meta-analysis)
title: Accuracy of MRI, MR arthrography, and ultrasound in the diagnosis of rotator cuff tears: a meta-analysis.
key_points: Meta-analysis of 65 articles with a surgical (open or arthroscopic) reference standard: MR arthrography was more sensitive and specific than MRI or ultrasound for both full- and partial-thickness rotator cuff tears (p < 0.05).
No significant differences in sensitivity or specificity between MRI and ultrasound for partial- or full-thickness tears (p > 0.05).
Area under the summary ROC curve for all tears: MR arthrography 0.935, ultrasound 0.889, MRI 0.878; pairwise comparison showed no significant difference between MRI and ultrasound (p > 0.05).
key_points_pt: Meta-análise de 65 artigos com padrão de referência cirúrgico (aberto ou artroscópico): a artro-RM foi mais sensível e específica do que a ressonância magnética ou a ecografia para roturas transfixivas e parciais da coifa dos rotadores (p < 0,05).
Sem diferenças significativas de sensibilidade ou especificidade entre ressonância magnética e ecografia para roturas parciais ou transfixivas (p > 0,05).

Área sob a curva ROC sumária para todas as roturas: artro-RM 0,935, ecografia 0,889, ressonância magnética 0,878; a comparação emparelhada não mostrou diferença significativa entre ressonância magnética e ecografia (p > 0,05).
abstract_excerpt: In diagnosing a full-thickness tear or a partial-thickness rotator cuff tear, MR arthrography is more sensitive and specific than either MRI or ultrasound (p < 0.05). There are no significant differences in either sensitivity or specificity between MRI and ultrasound in the diagnosis of partial- or full-thickness rotator cuff tears (p > 0.05). Summary ROC curves for MR arthrography, MRI, and ultrasound for all tears show the area under the ROC curve is greatest for MR arthrography (0.935), followed by ultrasound (0.889) and then MRI (0.878); however, pairwise comparisons of these curves show no significant differences between MRI and ultrasound (p > 0.05).

topic: Dynamic musculoskeletal ultrasound (illustrative review)
title: Musculoskeletal sonography: a dynamic tool for usual and unusual disorders.
key_points: Review illustrating a wide variety of musculoskeletal disorders that can be diagnosed with dynamic sonography.

Dynamic sonography is a useful tool for evaluating a variety of musculoskeletal disorders, many of which cannot be diagnosed by any other imaging method (qualitative conclusion; no accuracy figures in the abstract).
key_points_pt: Revisão que ilustra uma grande variedade de patologias musculoesqueléticas diagnosticáveis por ecografia dinâmica.

A ecografia dinâmica é uma ferramenta útil na avaliação de várias patologias musculoesqueléticas, muitas das quais não podem ser diagnosticadas por nenhum outro método de imagem (conclusão qualitativa; o resumo não apresenta valores de acuidade).
abstract_excerpt: OBJECTIVE: The purpose of this study is to illustrate a wide variety of musculoskeletal disorders that can be diagnosed with dynamic sonography. CONCLUSION: Dynamic sonography is a useful tool for the evaluation of a variety of musculoskeletal disorders. Many of these disorders cannot be diagnosed by any other imaging method.

topic: Dynamic ultrasound protocol for the shoulder (EURO-MUSCULUS/USPRM consensus)
title: EURO-MUSCULUS/USPRM Dynamic Ultrasound Protocols for Shoulder.
key_points: Practical guide prepared by an international consensus of experts (EURO-MUSCULUS and USPRM) describing dynamic ultrasound examination of the shoulder using different manoeuvres for several relevant shoulder problems.
Scanning videos are coupled with real-time patient examination videos, aiming at a better, uniform/standard approach (qualitative protocol; no accuracy figures in the abstract).
key_points_pt: Guia prático elaborado por consenso internacional de peritos (EURO-MUSCULUS e USPRM) que descreve o exame ecográfico dinâmico do ombro com diferentes manobras para vários problemas relevantes do ombro.

Os vídeos de aquisição ecográfica são associados a vídeos do exame do doente em tempo real, visando uma abordagem melhor e uniforme/padronizada (protocolo qualitativo; o resumo não apresenta valores de acuidade).
keywords: long head of biceps tendon instability
instabilidade do tendão da longa porção do bicípite
abstract_excerpt: In this dynamic protocol, ultrasound examination of the shoulder using different maneuvers is described for several/relevant shoulder problems. Scanning videos are coupled with real-time patient examination videos for better understanding. The authors believe that this practical guide prepared by an international consensus of several experts (EURO-MUSCULUS: European Musculoskeletal Ultrasound Study Group and USPRM: Ultrasound Study Group of ISPRM [International Society of Physical and Rehabilitation Medicine]) will help musculoskeletal physicians perform a better and uniform/standard approach.

topic: Pfirrmann MRI grading of lumbar disc degeneration
title: Magnetic resonance classification of lumbar intervertebral disc degeneration.
key_points: Five-grade (I-V) MRI classification of lumbar disc degeneration with a simple algorithm applied to routine T2-weighted images, tested on 300 discs in 60 patients by three observers.
Intraobserver kappa 0.84-0.90 and interobserver kappa 0.69-0.81; complete agreement in 83.8% of discs, one-grade difference in 15.9% and two or more grades in 1.3%.
Disc degeneration can be graded reliably on routine T2-weighted MR images.
key_points_pt: Classificação por ressonância magnética em cinco graus (I-V) da degenerescência discal lombar, com algoritmo simples aplicado a imagens ponderadas em T2 de rotina, testada em 300 discos de 60 doentes por três observadores.
Kappa intraobservador 0,84-0,90 e interobservador 0,69-0,81; concordância completa em 83,8% dos discos, diferença de um grau em 15,9% e de dois ou mais graus em 1,3%.
A degenerescência discal pode ser graduada de forma fiável em imagens de ressonância magnética ponderadas em T2 de rotina.
abstract_excerpt: There were 14 Grade I, 82 Grade II, 72 Grade III, 68 Grade IV, and 64 Grade V discs. The kappa coefficients for intra- and interobserver agreement were substantial to excellent: intraobserver (kappa range, 0.84-0.90) and interobserver (kappa range, 0.69-0.81). Complete agreement was obtained, on the average, in 83.8% of all the discs. A difference of one grade occurred in 15.9% and a difference of two or more grades in 1.3% of all the cases. CONCLUSION: Disc degeneration can be graded reliably on routine T2-weighted magnetic resonance images using the grading system and algorithm presented in this investigation.

topic: Modic vertebral endplate/marrow changes (original classification)
title: Degenerative disk disease: assessment of changes in vertebral body marrow with MR imaging.
key_points: In 474 consecutive lumbar MRI patients, type 1 changes (decreased T1 signal, increased T2 signal) were seen in 20 patients (4%) and type 2 changes (increased T1 signal, isointense or slightly increased T2 signal) in 77 patients (16%), always with degenerative disc disease at the involved level.
Histology (three cases of each type): type 1 showed disruption and fissuring of the end plates with vascularised fibrous tissue; type 2 showed yellow marrow replacement.
Longitudinally, type 1 changes converted to type 2 in five of six patients within 14 months to 3 years; type 2 changes in ten patients remained stable over 2-3 years.
key_points_pt: Em 474 doentes consecutivos submetidos a ressonância magnética lombar, observaram-se alterações tipo 1 (hipossinal em T1, hipersinal em T2) em 20 doentes (4%) e alterações tipo 2 (hipersinal em T1, isossinal ou ligeiro hipersinal em T2) em 77 doentes (16%), sempre associadas a discopatia degenerativa no nível envolvido.
Histologia (três casos de cada tipo): o tipo 1 mostrou rotura e fissuração dos planaltos vertebrais com tecido fibroso vascularizado; o tipo 2 mostrou substituição por medula amarela (gordurosa).
Longitudinalmente, as alterações tipo 1 converteram-se em tipo 2 em cinco de seis doentes em 14 meses a 3 anos; as alterações tipo 2 mantiveram-se estáveis em dez doentes durante 2-3 anos.
abstract_excerpt: Type 1 changes (decreased signal intensity on T1-weighted spin-echo images and increased signal intensity on T2-weighted images) were identified in 20 patients (4%) and type 2 (increased signal intensity on T1-weighted images and isointense or slightly increased signal intensity on T2-weighted images) in 77 patients (16%). In all cases there was evidence of associated degenerative disk disease at the level of involvement. Histopathologic sections in three cases of type 1 change demonstrated disruption and fissuring of the end plates and vascularized fibrous tissue, while in three cases of type 2 change they demonstrated yellow marrow replacement. ... Type 1 changes in five of six patients converted to a type 2 pattern in 14 months to 3 years. Type 2 changes in ten patients remained stable over a 2-3-year period.

topic: Lumbar disc nomenclature version 2.0 (NASS/ASSR/ASNR consensus)
title: Lumbar disc nomenclature: version 2.0: Recommendations of the combined task forces of the North American Spine Society, the American Society of Spine Radiology and the American Society of Neuroradiology.
key_points: Revised (version 2.0) lumbar disc nomenclature representing consensus recommendations of the combined task forces of the ASSR, ASNR and NASS, updating the 2001 document (also published in Spine 2014, PMID 23970106).
Recommended diagnostic categories: normal; congenital/developmental variation; degeneration; trauma; infection/inflammation; neoplasia; and/or morphologic variant of uncertain significance.

Provides a glossary of lumbar disc terms with their recommended usage, describing terms as preferred, nonpreferred, nonstandard and colloquial; the nomenclature is intended to serve as a system for classification and reporting.
key_points_pt: Nomenclatura revista (versão 2.0) do disco lombar que representa as recomendações de consenso dos grupos de trabalho conjuntos da ASSR, ASNR e NASS, atualizando o documento de 2001 (também publicada na Spine 2014, PMID 23970106).
Categorias diagnósticas recomendadas: normal; variante congénita/do desenvolvimento; degenerescência; trauma; infeção/inflamação; neoplasia; e/ou variante morfológica de significado incerto.

Inclui um glossário de termos do disco lombar com a respetiva utilização recomendada, classificando os termos como preferidos, não preferidos, não padronizados e coloquiais; a nomenclatura destina-se a servir como sistema de classificação e de relatório.
abstract_excerpt: The article provides a discussion of the recommended diagnostic categories pertaining to the lumbar disc: normal; congenital/developmental variation; degeneration; trauma; infection/inflammation; neoplasia; and/or morphologic variant of uncertain significance. The article provides a glossary of terms pertaining to the lumbar disc, a detailed discussion of these terms, and their recommended usage. Terms are described as preferred, nonpreferred, nonstandard, and colloquial. ... We have revised and updated a document that, since 2001, has provided a widely acceptable nomenclature that helps maintain consistency and accuracy in the description of the anatomic and physiologic properties of the normal and abnormal lumbar disc and that serves as a system for classification and reporting built upon that nomenclature.

topic: Prevalence of Modic/endplate signal changes and association with low back pain (systematic review)
title: Vertebral endplate signal changes (Modic change): a systematic literature review of prevalence and association with non-specific low back pain.
key_points: Systematic review of 82 study samples from 77 articles: median reported prevalence of any vertebral endplate signal change (including Modic changes) was 43% in patients with non-specific low back pain and/or sciatica and 6% in non-clinical populations.
Prevalence was positively associated with age; a positive association with non-specific low back pain was found in seven of ten studies, with odds ratios from 2.0 to 19.9.
Endplate signal changes are common in non-specific low back pain and associated with pain, but may also be present in individuals without low back pain.
key_points_pt: Revisão sistemática de 82 amostras de 77 artigos: a prevalência mediana reportada de qualquer alteração de sinal dos planaltos vertebrais (incluindo alterações de Modic) foi de 43% em doentes com lombalgia inespecífica e/ou ciatalgia e de 6% em populações não clínicas.
A prevalência associou-se positivamente com a idade; verificou-se associação positiva com lombalgia inespecífica em sete de dez estudos, com odds ratios de 2,0 a 19,9.
As alterações de sinal dos planaltos vertebrais são frequentes na lombalgia inespecífica e associam-se a dor, mas podem também estar presentes em indivíduos sem lombalgia.
keywords: alterações de sinal dos planaltos vertebrais
abstract_excerpt: The median of the reported prevalence rates for any type of VESC was 43% in patients with non-specific LBP and/or sciatica and 6% in non-clinical populations. The prevalence was positively associated with age and was negatively associated with the overall quality of the studies. A positive association between VESC and non-specific LBP was found in seven of ten studies from the general, working, and clinical populations with ORs from 2.0 to 19.9. This systematic review shows that VESC is a common MRI-finding in patients with non-specific LBP and is associated with pain. However, it should be noted that VESC may be present in individuals without LBP.

topic: Prevalence of degenerative spine imaging findings in asymptomatic people (systematic review)
title: Systematic literature review of imaging features of spinal degeneration in asymptomatic populations.
key_points: Systematic review of 33 articles (3110 asymptomatic individuals, CT or MRI): prevalence of disc degeneration increased from 37% at 20 years of age to 96% at 80 years.
From age 20 to 80 in asymptomatic individuals: disc bulge 30% to 84%, disc protrusion 29% to 43%, annular fissure 19% to 29%.
Many imaging-based degenerative features are likely part of normal ageing and unassociated with pain, and must be interpreted in the context of the patient's clinical condition.
key_points_pt: Revisão sistemática de 33 artigos (3110 indivíduos assintomáticos, TC ou ressonância magnética): a prevalência de degenerescência discal aumentou de 37% aos 20 anos para 96% aos 80 anos.
Dos 20 aos 80 anos em indivíduos assintomáticos: abaulamento discal de 30% para 84%, protrusão discal de 29% para 43%, fissura do anel fibroso de 19% para 29%.
Muitos achados degenerativos imagiológicos fazem provavelmente parte do envelhecimento normal e não se associam a dor, devendo ser interpretados no contexto clínico do doente.
abstract_excerpt: The prevalence of disk degeneration in asymptomatic individuals increased from 37% of 20-year-old individuals to 96% of 80-year-old individuals. Disk bulge prevalence increased from 30% of those 20 years of age to 84% of those 80 years of age. Disk protrusion prevalence increased from 29% of those 20 years of age to 43% of those 80 years of age. The prevalence of annular fissure increased from 19% of those 20 years of age to 29% of those 80 years of age. CONCLUSIONS: Imaging findings of spine degeneration are present in high proportions of asymptomatic individuals, increasing with age. Many imaging-based degenerative features are likely part of normal aging and unassociated with pain. These imaging findings must be interpreted in the context of the patient's clinical condition.

topic: Lodwick radiographic grading of focal bone lesions (growth rate)
title: Determining growth rates of focal lesions of bone from radiographs.
key_points: Radiographic grading of focal bone lesions as an expression of growth rate; rate of growth divides focal bone lesions into two largely mutually exclusive classes.

Grading helps decide which lesions should be biopsied and which may be safely followed; a set of rules establishes each of five grades in the presence of bone destruction (qualitative; no accuracy figures in the abstract).
key_points_pt: Graduação radiográfica das lesões ósseas focais como expressão da taxa de crescimento; a taxa de crescimento divide as lesões ósseas focais em duas classes largamente mutuamente exclusivas.

A graduação ajuda a decidir que lesões devem ser biopsadas e quais podem ser vigiadas com segurança; um conjunto de regras define cada um dos cinco graus na presença de destruição óssea (qualitativo; o resumo não apresenta valores de acuidade).
abstract_excerpt: Rate of growth divides focal lesions of bone into two classes which are largely mutually exclusive. Not all focal lesions require biopsy, and grading is especially helpful in deciding which should be biopsied and which may be safely followed. The statistical proof and logic of grading as an expression of growth rate are presented with a set of rules establishing each of the five grades in the presence of bone destruction.

topic: Modified Lodwick-Madewell grading of lytic bone lesions
title: A Modified Lodwick-Madewell Grading System for the Evaluation of Lytic Bone Lesions.
key_points: Retrospective review of radiographs of 183 bone lesions (selected to include a broad range of benign and malignant tumours) using a three-grade Modified Lodwick-Madewell system: grade I (Lodwick IA and IB), grade II (Lodwick IC), grade III (changing margination, moth-eaten and permeative patterns, radiographically occult); 81 lesions were grade I, 54 grade II and 48 grade III.
76 of 81 (94%) grade I lesions were benign and 39 of 48 (81%) grade III lesions were malignant; grade II lesions were split nearly equally between benign and malignant.
Grade I lesions are usually benign, grade II lesions carry moderate risk of malignancy, and grade III lesions have a high likelihood of malignancy.
key_points_pt: Revisão retrospetiva de radiografias de 183 lesões ósseas (selecionadas para incluir um amplo espetro de tumores benignos e malignos) com o sistema de Lodwick-Madewell modificado em três graus: grau I (Lodwick IA e IB), grau II (Lodwick IC), grau III (margens em mudança, padrões roído de traça e permeativo, lesão radiograficamente oculta); 81 lesões foram de grau I, 54 de grau II e 48 de grau III.
76 de 81 (94%) lesões de grau I eram benignas e 39 de 48 (81%) lesões de grau III eram malignas; as lesões de grau II dividiram-se de forma quase igual entre benignas e malignas.
As lesões de grau I são habitualmente benignas, as de grau II têm risco moderado de malignidade e as de grau III têm elevada probabilidade de malignidade.
abstract_excerpt: This modified system consists of grade I, which is composed of grades IA and IB as listed in the Lodwick system; grade II, which is grade IC in the Lodwick system; and grade III, which is composed of IIIA (changing margination), IIB (moth-eaten and permeative patterns), and IIIC (radiographically occult). ... Of the 183 tumors, 81 were classified as grade I, 54 as grade II, and 48 as grade III. When correlating grade with pathology, we found that 76 of 81 (94%) grade I lesions were benign and 39 of 48 grade III lesions (81%) were malignant. ... Grade I lesions are usually benign, grade II lesions carry moderate risk of malignancy, and grade III lesions possess a high likelihood of malignancy.

topic: ACR Appropriateness Criteria: Suspected Primary Bone Tumors (2024 update)
authors: Expert Panel on Musculoskeletal Imaging; Ahlawat S, et al.
title: ACR Appropriateness Criteria® Suspected Primary Bone Tumors: 2024 Update.
key_points: Radiographs are the most appropriate initial imaging study for detection and characterisation of the majority of primary bone tumours and often provide sufficient information for diagnosis.
For radiographically occult primary bone tumours, MRI and/or CT can be performed.
For indeterminate or aggressive bone tumours on radiographs, MRI or CT are typically the most appropriate next step to evaluate anatomic extent, viability and to plan biopsy or surgery.
key_points_pt: A radiografia é o exame inicial mais apropriado para deteção e caracterização da maioria dos tumores ósseos primários e frequentemente fornece informação suficiente para o diagnóstico.
Nos tumores ósseos primários radiograficamente ocultos, pode realizar-se ressonância magnética e/ou TC.

Nos tumores ósseos indeterminados ou agressivos na radiografia, a ressonância magnética ou a TC são tipicamente o passo seguinte mais apropriado para avaliar a extensão anatómica, a viabilidade e planear a biópsia ou a cirurgia.
abstract_excerpt: Radiographs are the most appropriate initial imaging study for detection and characterization of the majority of primary bone tumors. Radiographs often provide sufficient information for the diagnosis of primary bone tumors, however, for radiographically occult primary bone tumors, MRI and/or CT can be performed. For indeterminate or aggressive bone tumors on radiographs, MRI or CT are typically the most appropriate next step for the evaluation of anatomic extent, assessment of viability and biopsy or surgical planning.

topic: ACR Bone-RADS risk stratification of bone lesions on radiography
title: Bone Tumor Risk Stratification and Management System: A Consensus Guideline from the ACR Bone Reporting and Data System Committee.
key_points: ACR Bone-RADS committee consensus scoring system to stratify a newly identified, potentially neoplastic bone lesion on radiography, viewed in the proper clinical context, as very low, low, intermediate or high risk of malignancy (Bone-RADS score 1-4).

Radiographic risk features each receive a point value: margination, pattern of periosteal reaction, depth of endosteal erosion, pathological fracture and extra-osseous soft tissue mass; the summed points translate to the Bone-RADS score.
Evidence-based and best-practice consensus management suggestions are given for each score, with a standardised diagnostic radiography report template.
key_points_pt: Sistema de pontuação de consenso do comité ACR Bone-RADS para estratificar uma lesão óssea potencialmente neoplásica recém-identificada na radiografia, analisada no contexto clínico adequado, em risco de malignidade muito baixo, baixo, intermédio ou elevado (Bone-RADS 1-4).

Cada achado radiográfico de risco recebe uma pontuação: margens, padrão de reação periosteal, profundidade da erosão endosteal, fratura patológica e massa de tecidos moles extraóssea; a soma dos pontos traduz-se na categoria Bone-RADS.
São propostas recomendações de orientação baseadas na evidência e no consenso para cada categoria, com um modelo padronizado de relatório radiográfico.
keywords: estratificação de risco de lesão óssea
abstract_excerpt: When viewed in the proper clinical context, a newly identified bone lesion can be risk stratified as having very low, low, intermediate, or high risk of malignancy. Radiographic features predictive of risk are reviewed include margination, pattern of periosteal reaction, depth of endosteal erosion, pathological fracture, and extra-osseous soft tissue mass. ... To apply the Bone-RADS scoring system to a potentially neoplastic bone lesion, radiographic features predictive of risk are each given a point value. Point values are summed to yield a point total, which can be translated to a Bone-RADS score (1-4) with corresponding risk assignment (very low, low, intermediate, high). For each score, evidence-based and best practice consensus management suggestions are outlined. ... a standardized diagnostic radiography report template is provided.

topic: ACR Appropriateness Criteria: Suspected Osteomyelitis of the Foot in Diabetes Mellitus (2025 update)
authors: Expert Panel on Musculoskeletal Imaging; Baker JC, et al.
title: ACR Appropriateness Criteria® Suspected Osteomyelitis of the Foot in Patients With Diabetes Mellitus: 2025 Update.
key_points: Foot infection is a common cause of diabetes-related morbidity, with 20% of patients with diabetic foot ulcers going on to develop osteomyelitis.
Radiography of the foot is recommended for the initial imaging evaluation of suspected foot osteomyelitis in adults with diabetes mellitus.

When initial radiographs are negative or indeterminate, or positive and treatment planning is needed, MRI of the foot is most commonly the recommended next study; metal instrumentation can alter recommendations in select cases.
key_points_pt: A infeção do pé é uma causa frequente de morbilidade relacionada com a diabetes, e 20% dos doentes com úlceras do pé diabético desenvolvem osteomielite.
A radiografia do pé é recomendada para a avaliação imagiológica inicial da suspeita de osteomielite do pé em adultos com diabetes mellitus.

Quando as radiografias iniciais são negativas ou indeterminadas, ou positivas com necessidade de planeamento terapêutico, a ressonância magnética do pé é habitualmente o exame seguinte recomendado; a presença de material metálico pode alterar as recomendações em casos selecionados.
abstract_excerpt: Foot infection is a common cause of diabetes-related morbidity, with 20% of patients with diabetic foot ulcers going on to develop osteomyelitis. Radiography of the foot is recommended for the initial imaging evaluation for suspected osteomyelitis of the foot in adult patients with diabetes mellitus. When initial radiographs are negative or indeterminate or when radiographs are positive for osteomyelitis and treatment planning is necessary, the recommended next imaging study is most commonly MRI of the foot. The presence of metal instrumentation in the foot can alter recommendations in select cases.

topic: Imaging accuracy for osteomyelitis in diabetic foot ulcers (meta-analysis)
title: Imaging for detection of osteomyelitis in people with diabetic foot ulcers: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
key_points: Meta-analysis of 36 studies (eight at high risk of bias): MRI had high diagnostic accuracy for osteomyelitis in diabetic foot ulcers (22 studies: sensitivity 96.4% [95% CI 90.7-98.7], specificity 83.8% [76.0-89.5]).
Radiographs had generally inferior accuracy (16 studies: sensitivity 61.9% [50.5-72.1], specificity 78.3% [62.9-88.5]); scintigraphy 84.2% [76.8-89.6] / 67.7% [56.2-77.4] (17 studies).
PET also had high accuracy (6 studies: sensitivity 84.3% [52.8-96.3], specificity 92.8% [75.7-98.2]); MRI may be the preferable test in most cases given wider availability and no ionising radiation.
key_points_pt: Meta-análise de 36 estudos (oito com risco de viés elevado): a ressonância magnética teve elevada acuidade diagnóstica para osteomielite em úlceras do pé diabético (22 estudos: sensibilidade 96,4% [IC 95% 90,7-98,7], especificidade 83,8% [76,0-89,5]).
A radiografia teve acuidade globalmente inferior (16 estudos: sensibilidade 61,9% [50,5-72,1], especificidade 78,3% [62,9-88,5]); cintigrafia 84,2% [76,8-89,6] / 67,7% [56,2-77,4] (17 estudos).

A PET também teve elevada acuidade (6 estudos: sensibilidade 84,3% [52,8-96,3], especificidade 92,8% [75,7-98,2]); a ressonância magnética poderá ser o exame preferível na maioria dos casos, dada a maior disponibilidade e a ausência de radiação ionizante.
abstract_excerpt: Thirty-six studies were included in the meta-analysis. Eight studies were at high risk of bias MRI had high diagnostic accuracy (22 studies: 96.4 % sensitivity (95 % CI 90.7-98.7); 83.8 % specificity (76.0-89.5)). PET scans also had high accuracy (6 studies: 84.3 % sensitivity (52.8-96.3); 92.8 % specificity (75.7-98.2)) ... Scintigraphy (17 studies: 84.2 % sensitivity (76.8-89.6); 67.7 % specificity (56.2-77.4)), and X-rays (16 studies: 61.9 % sensitivity (50.5-72.1); 78.3 % specificity (62.9-88.5)) had generally inferior diagnostic accuracy. ... MRI may be the preferable test in most cases, given its wider availability and the lack of potentially harmful ionising radiation.

topic: Warwick Agreement on femoroacetabular impingement syndrome
title: The Warwick Agreement on femoroacetabular impingement syndrome (FAI syndrome): an international consensus statement.
key_points: International multidisciplinary consensus (22 panel members and 1 patient from 9 countries and 5 specialties) introduced the term 'femoroacetabular impingement syndrome' to reflect the central role of symptoms.
To reach a diagnosis of FAI syndrome, patients should have appropriate symptoms, positive clinical signs and imaging findings (imaging findings are one of three required elements).
Suitable treatments are conservative care, rehabilitation, and arthroscopic or open surgery.
key_points_pt: Consenso internacional multidisciplinar (22 membros do painel e 1 doente de 9 países e 5 especialidades) introduziu o termo 'síndrome de conflito femoroacetabular' para refletir o papel central dos sintomas.

Para o diagnóstico de síndrome de conflito femoroacetabular, os doentes devem apresentar sintomas adequados, sinais clínicos positivos e achados imagiológicos (os achados imagiológicos são um dos três elementos necessários).
Os tratamentos adequados são o tratamento conservador, a reabilitação e a cirurgia artroscópica ou aberta.
abstract_excerpt: 22 panel members and 1 patient from 9 countries and 5 different specialties participated in a 1-day consensus meeting on 29 June 2016. ... The term 'femoroacetabular impingement syndrome' was introduced to reflect the central role of patients' symptoms in the disorder. To reach a diagnosis, patients should have appropriate symptoms, positive clinical signs and imaging findings. Suitable treatments are conservative care, rehabilitation, and arthroscopic or open surgery.

topic: Lisbon Agreement on FAI imaging: parameters and reporting (alpha angle, LCEA/Wiberg)
title: The Lisbon Agreement on femoroacetabular impingement imaging-part 2: general issues, parameters, and reporting.
key_points: Delphi consensus of 30 panel members from 13 countries: 47 statements generated with group consensus for 45; 25 statements cover 'General issues' and 'Parameters and reporting'.

Radiographic evaluation (AP pelvis and Dunn 45° view) is the cornerstone and the minimum imaging study when evaluating adults for FAI; in most cases cross-sectional imaging is warranted because MRI is the 'gold standard' for comprehensive evaluation, differential diagnosis and surgical planning.

Acetabular coverage (Wiberg's angle and acetabular index) and version (crossover, posterior wall and ischial spine signs) should be assessed routinely; on the femoral side, head-neck junction morphology (alpha angle and offset), neck-shaft angle and torsion should be assessed.
key_points_pt: Consenso Delphi de 30 peritos de 13 países: 47 afirmações geradas, com consenso de grupo em 45; 25 afirmações abordam 'Questões gerais' e 'Parâmetros e relatório'.

A avaliação radiográfica (radiografia AP da bacia e incidência de Dunn a 45°) é a base e o estudo imagiológico mínimo na avaliação de adultos com suspeita de conflito femoroacetabular; na maioria dos casos justifica-se imagem seccional, pois a ressonância magnética é o 'padrão de referência' para avaliação abrangente, diagnóstico diferencial e planeamento cirúrgico.

A cobertura acetabular (ângulo de Wiberg e índice acetabular) e a versão acetabular (sinais do cruzamento, da parede posterior e da espinha isquiática) devem ser avaliadas por rotina; no fémur, devem avaliar-se a morfologia da junção cabeça-colo (ângulo alfa e offset), o ângulo cervicodiafisário e a torção femoral.
abstract_excerpt: Forty-seven statements were generated and group consensus was reached for 45. Twenty-five statements pertaining to 'General issues' (9 addressing diagnosis, differential diagnosis, and postoperative imaging) and 'Parameters and reporting' (16 addressing femoral/acetabular parameters) were produced. ... Radiographic evaluation (AP pelvis and a Dunn 45° view) is the cornerstone of hip-imaging assessment and the minimum imaging study that should be performed when evaluating adult patients for FAI. In most cases, cross-sectional imaging is warranted because MRI is the 'gold standard' imaging modality for the comprehensive evaluation, differential diagnosis assessment, and FAI surgical planning. ... • For acetabular morphology, coverage (Wiberg's angle and acetabular index) and version (crossover, posterior wall, and ischial spine signs) should be assessed routinely. On the femoral side, the head-neck junction morphology (α° and offset), neck morphology (NSA), and torsion should be assessed.

topic: Alpha angle of the femoral head-neck junction (cam morphology), original description
title: The contour of the femoral head-neck junction as a predictor for the risk of anterior impingement.
key_points: Developed the alpha angle, measured on tilted axial MRI through the centre of the femoral head, to describe concavity at the femoral head-neck junction (case-control study: 39 symptomatic patients vs 35 asymptomatic controls).
The alpha angle averaged 74.0° in patients with clinical impingement vs 42.0° in controls (p < 0.001); repeated measurements showed good reproducibility among four observers.
key_points_pt: Desenvolveu o ângulo alfa, medido em cortes axiais oblíquos de ressonância magnética através do centro da cabeça femoral, para descrever a concavidade da junção cabeça-colo femoral (estudo caso-controlo: 39 doentes sintomáticos vs 35 controlos assintomáticos).
O ângulo alfa médio foi de 74,0° nos doentes com conflito clínico vs 42,0° nos controlos (p < 0,001); as medições repetidas mostraram boa reprodutibilidade entre quatro observadores.
abstract_excerpt: MR scans of 39 patients with groin pain, decreased internal rotation and a positive impingement test were compared with those of 35 asymptomatic control subjects. The waist of the femoral head-neck junction was identified on tilted axial MR scans passing through the centre of the head. The anterior margin of the waist of the femoral neck was defined and measured by an angle (alpha). ... Repeated measurements showed good reproducibility among four observers. The angle alpha averaged 74.0 degrees for the patients and 42.0 degrees for the control group (p < 0.001).

topic: Radiographic reference values for acetabular under- and overcoverage (LCEA, acetabular index)
title: What are the radiographic reference values for acetabular under- and overcoverage?
key_points: Retrospective comparison of 11 radiographic parameters on AP pelvic radiographs among hip dysplasia (26 hips), controls (21), overcoverage (14) and severe overcoverage/protrusio (25), corrected for neutral pelvic orientation using a true lateral radiograph.

Reference values: lateral centre-edge angle 23° to 33°, medial centre-edge angle 35° to 44°, acetabular index 3° to 13°, extrusion index 17% to 27%, Sharp angle 38° to 42°, acetabular arc 61° to 65°, negative crossover sign, positive posterior wall sign.
From dysplasia through control and overcoverage, the lateral centre-edge angle increased while the medial centre-edge angle, extrusion index, acetabular index and Sharp angle decreased.
key_points_pt: Comparação retrospetiva de 11 parâmetros em radiografias AP da bacia entre ancas displásicas (26), controlos (21), com sobrecobertura (14) e com sobrecobertura grave/protrusão acetabular (25), corrigidos para orientação pélvica neutra com recurso a uma radiografia de perfil verdadeiro.

Valores de referência: ângulo centro-bordo lateral 23° a 33°, ângulo centro-bordo medial 35° a 44°, índice acetabular 3° a 13°, índice de extrusão 17% a 27%, ângulo de Sharp 38° a 42°, arco acetabular 61° a 65°, sinal do cruzamento negativo, sinal da parede posterior positivo.

Da displasia para os controlos e para a sobrecobertura, o ângulo centro-bordo lateral aumentou, enquanto o ângulo centro-bordo medial, o índice de extrusão, o índice acetabular e o ângulo de Sharp diminuíram.
abstract_excerpt: From dysplasia through control and overcoverage, the lateral center-edge angle, acetabular arc, and anteroposterior/craniocaudal coverage increased. In contrast, the medial center-edge angle, extrusion/acetabular index, Sharp angle, and prevalence of the posterior wall sign decreased. The following reference values were found: lateral center-edge angle 23° to 33°, medial center-edge angle 35° to 44°, acetabular arc 61° to 65°, extrusion index 17% to 27%, acetabular index 3° to 13°, Sharp angle 38° to 42°, negative crossover sign, positive posterior wall sign, anterior femoral head coverage 15% to 26%, posterior femoral head coverage 36% to 47%, and craniocaudal coverage 70% to 83%.

topic: General multimodal LLMs (GPT-4V, Gemini Pro Vision) vs radiologists on image-input differential diagnosis
authors: Suh PS, Shim WH, Suh CH, et al.
title: Comparing Diagnostic Accuracy of Radiologists versus GPT-4V and Gemini Pro Vision Using Image Inputs from Diagnosis Please Cases
key_points: Retrospective study of 190 Radiology 'Diagnosis Please' cases (2008-2023), including 17 musculoskeletal cases. GPT-4V and Gemini Pro Vision received the original images plus captures of the patient history and figure legends (without imaging findings). They were asked for three differential diagnoses, repeated five times at temperatures 0, 0.5 and 1. Eight subspecialty-trained radiologists also solved the cases.

At temperature 1, overall accuracy was 49% (93/190) for GPT-4V and 39% (74/190) for Gemini Pro Vision, versus 61% (115/190) for radiologists. Radiologists outperformed Gemini Pro Vision (P < .001); the difference versus GPT-4V was not statistically significant after Bonferroni adjustment (P = .02).
Radiologists (range, 45%-88%) outperformed the LLMs at temperature 1 (range, 24%-75%) in most subspecialties.

A case was scored correct if the generated diagnoses included the final diagnosis after five repetitions. Accuracy rose with temperature (GPT-4V 41%, 45% and 49%; Gemini Pro Vision 29%, 36% and 39% at 0, 0.5 and 1), but the trend was not significant after Bonferroni adjustment.
key_points_pt: Estudo retrospetivo de 190 casos 'Diagnosis Please' da revista Radiology (2008-2023), incluindo 17 casos musculoesqueléticos. O GPT-4V e o Gemini Pro Vision receberam as imagens originais e capturas da história clínica e das legendas das figuras (sem os achados imagiológicos). Foram-lhes pedidos três diagnósticos diferenciais, repetidos cinco vezes com temperaturas 0, 0,5 e 1. Oito radiologistas com formação subespecializada resolveram também os casos.

Com temperatura 1, a exatidão global foi de 49% (93/190) para o GPT-4V e de 39% (74/190) para o Gemini Pro Vision, face a 61% (115/190) para os radiologistas. Os radiologistas superaram o Gemini Pro Vision (P < 0,001); a diferença face ao GPT-4V não foi estatisticamente significativa após correção de Bonferroni (P = 0,02).
Os radiologistas (intervalo 45%-88%) superaram os modelos de linguagem com temperatura 1 (intervalo 24%-75%) na maioria das subespecialidades.

Um caso foi considerado correto se os diagnósticos gerados incluíssem o diagnóstico final ao fim de cinco repetições. A exatidão aumentou com a temperatura (GPT-4V 41%, 45% e 49%; Gemini Pro Vision 29%, 36% e 39% com 0, 0,5 e 1), mas a tendência não foi significativa após correção de Bonferroni.
abstract_excerpt: Overall accuracy improved with increasing temperature settings (0, 0.5, 1) for both GPT-4V (41% [78 of 190 cases], 45% [86 of 190 cases], 49% [93 of 190 cases], respectively) and Gemini Pro Vision (29% [55 of 190 cases], 36% [69 of 190 cases], 39% [74 of 190 cases], respectively), although there was no evidence of a statistically significant difference after Bonferroni adjustment (GPT-4V, P = .12; Gemini Pro Vision, P = .04). The overall accuracy of radiologists (61% [115 of 190 cases]) was higher than that of Gemini Pro Vision at temperature 1 (T1) (P < .001), while no statistically significant difference was observed between radiologists and GPT-4V at T1 after Bonferroni adjustment (P = .02). Radiologists (range, 45%-88%) outperformed the LLMs at T1 (range, 24%-75%) in most subspecialties.

topic: GPT-4V image input vs GPT-4 text input vs radiologists in musculoskeletal radiology cases
authors: Horiuchi D, Tatekawa H, Oura T, et al.
title: ChatGPT's diagnostic performance based on textual vs. visual information compared to radiologists' diagnostic performance in musculoskeletal radiology
key_points: Across 106 musculoskeletal 'Test Yourself' cases from Skeletal Radiology, GPT-4V-based ChatGPT given the medical history and images reached 8% (9/106) diagnostic accuracy. GPT-4-based ChatGPT given the medical history and textual imaging findings reached 43% (46/106) (p < 0.001).

A radiology resident scored 41% (43/106) and a board-certified radiologist 53% (56/106). GPT-4V was significantly less accurate than both (p < 0.001); text-based GPT-4 did not differ significantly from either (p = 0.78 and 0.22).
The authors conclude that ChatGPT should be given appropriate descriptions of the imaging findings rather than the images themselves.
key_points_pt: Em 106 casos musculoesqueléticos 'Test Yourself' da revista Skeletal Radiology, o ChatGPT baseado no GPT-4V, com história clínica e imagens, atingiu 8% (9/106) de exatidão diagnóstica. O ChatGPT baseado no GPT-4, com história clínica e descrição textual dos achados imagiológicos, atingiu 43% (46/106) (p < 0,001).

Um interno de radiologia obteve 41% (43/106) e um radiologista especialista 53% (56/106). O GPT-4V foi significativamente menos exato do que ambos (p < 0,001); o GPT-4 com texto não diferiu significativamente de nenhum deles (p = 0,78 e 0,22).
Os autores concluem que se deve fornecer ao ChatGPT uma descrição adequada dos achados imagiológicos, e não as próprias imagens.
abstract_excerpt: GPT-4-based ChatGPT significantly outperformed GPT-4V-based ChatGPT (p < 0.001) with accuracy rates of 43% (46/106) and 8% (9/106), respectively. The radiology resident and the board-certified radiologist achieved accuracy rates of 41% (43/106) and 53% (56/106). The diagnostic accuracy of GPT-4-based ChatGPT was comparable to that of the radiology resident, but was lower than that of the board-certified radiologist although the differences were not significant (p = 0.78 and 0.22, respectively). The diagnostic accuracy of GPT-4V-based ChatGPT was significantly lower than those of both radiologists (p < 0.001 and < 0.001, respectively). ... When utilizing ChatGPT, it is crucial to input appropriate descriptions of imaging findings rather than the images.

topic: Claude 3 Opus / Claude 3.5 Sonnet diagnostic performance with history, textual findings or key images
authors: Kurokawa R, Ohizumi Y, Kanzawa J, et al.
title: Diagnostic performances of Claude 3 Opus and Claude 3.5 Sonnet from patient history and key images in Radiology's "Diagnosis Please" cases
key_points: Claude 3 Opus and Claude 3.5 Sonnet were tested on 322 Radiology 'Diagnosis Please' cases under three input conditions: (1) clinical history only; (2) history plus the submitter's textual imaging findings; (3) history plus key images (PNG).

Correct diagnosis rates (Opus / 3.5 Sonnet) were 18.0% / 21.4% with history only, 62.4% / 64.9% with history plus textual findings, and 24.8% / 30.1% with history plus key images. Differences among all conditions were significant (p < 0.01).

Key images improved accuracy over history alone, but stayed far below the accuracy reached when the submitter's textual description of the imaging findings was provided (24.8% / 30.1% vs 62.4% / 64.9%).
Claude 3.5 Sonnet was significantly better than Claude 3 Opus only with image input (30.1% vs 24.8%, p = 0.028).
key_points_pt: O Claude 3 Opus e o Claude 3.5 Sonnet foram testados em 322 casos 'Diagnosis Please' da revista Radiology, em três condições de entrada: (1) apenas história clínica; (2) história e achados imagiológicos descritos em texto pelo autor do caso; (3) história e imagens-chave (PNG).

As taxas de diagnóstico correto (Opus / 3.5 Sonnet) foram de 18,0% / 21,4% apenas com a história, 62,4% / 64,9% com a história e os achados em texto, e 24,8% / 30,1% com a história e as imagens-chave. Todas as diferenças entre condições foram significativas (p < 0,01).

As imagens-chave melhoraram a exatidão face à história isolada, mas ficaram muito aquém da exatidão obtida quando foi fornecida a descrição textual dos achados imagiológicos feita pelo autor do caso (24,8% / 30,1% vs. 62,4% / 64,9%).
O Claude 3.5 Sonnet foi significativamente superior ao Claude 3 Opus apenas com entrada de imagens (30,1% vs. 24,8%, p = 0,028).
abstract_excerpt: The correct diagnosis rates were 58/322 (18.0%) and 69/322 (21.4%), 201/322 (62.4%) and 209/322 (64.9%), and 80/322 (24.8%) and 97/322 (30.1%) for Conditions 1, 2, and 3 for Claude 3 Opus and Claude 3.5 Sonnet, respectively. The models provided the correct answer as a differential diagnosis in up to 26/322 (8.1%) for Opus and 23/322 (7.1%) for Sonnet. Statistically significant differences were observed in the correct response rates among all combinations of Conditions 1, 2, and 3 for each model (p < 0.01). Claude 3.5 Sonnet outperformed in all conditions, but a statistically significant difference was observed only in the comparison for Condition 3 (30.1% vs. 24.8%, p = 0.028).

topic: GPT-4V performance on text- vs image-based radiology examination questions
authors: Hayden N, Gilbert S, Poisson LM, et al.
title: Performance of GPT-4 with Vision on Text- and Image-based ACR Diagnostic Radiology In-Training Examination Questions
key_points: Prospective evaluation of the September 2023 release of GPT-4V on 377 unique retired ACR Diagnostic Radiology In-Training Examination questions: 65.3% (246/377) answered correctly.
Accuracy was significantly higher on text-only questions (81.5%, 159/195) than on image-based questions (47.8%, 87/182) (P < .001).

On text-based questions, chain-of-thought prompting outperformed the other prompts by 6.1%-8.9% (FDR 0.014-0.063). On image-based questions, prompts made no difference (P = .27 to >.99). The authors conclude that GPT-4V showed deficits interpreting radiologic images.
key_points_pt: Avaliação prospetiva da versão de setembro de 2023 do GPT-4V em 377 perguntas únicas, já retiradas, dos exames de treino (In-Training Examination) de Radiologia de Diagnóstico do ACR: 65,3% (246/377) de respostas corretas.
A exatidão foi significativamente superior nas perguntas só de texto (81,5%, 159/195) do que nas perguntas com imagem (47,8%, 87/182) (P < 0,001).

Nas perguntas de texto, o prompting com cadeia de raciocínio (chain-of-thought) superou os outros prompts em 6,1%-8,9% (FDR 0,014-0,063). Nas perguntas com imagem, os prompts não fizeram diferença (P = 0,27 a >0,99). Os autores concluem que o GPT-4V revelou défices na interpretação de imagens radiológicas.
abstract_excerpt: GPT-4V correctly answered 246 (65.3%) of the 377 unique questions, with significantly higher accuracy on text-only questions (81.5%, 159 of 195) than on image-based questions (47.8%, 87 of 182) (χ2 test, P < .001). Subanalysis revealed differences between prompts on text-based questions, where chain-of-thought prompting outperformed long instruction by 6.1% (McNemar, P = .02; FDR = 0.063), basic prompting by 6.8% (P = .009, FDR = 0.044), and the original prompting style by 8.9% (P = .001, FDR = 0.014). No differences were observed between prompts on image-based questions with P values of .27 to >.99. Conclusion While GPT-4V demonstrated a level of competence in text-based questions, it showed deficits interpreting radiologic images.

topic: GPT-4V hallucination (fabricated findings), context dependence and instability in radiologic image interpretation
authors: Huppertz MS, Siepmann R, Topp D, et al.
title: Revolution or risk?-Assessing the potential and challenges of GPT-4V in radiologic image interpretation
key_points: GPT-4V read 206 imaging studies with unequivocal findings (60 radiographs, 60 CT, 60 MRI, 26 angiographies) twice: with the image only, and with added clinical and demographic context.

Diagnostic accuracy was 8.3% without context, 29.1% with context (first diagnosis correct) and 63.6% with context (correct diagnosis among the differentials) (p ≤ 0.001). The authors attribute this to a pronounced tendency to favour context over image information.
GPT-4V fabricated 258 imaging findings in 412 responses and misidentified the imaging modality or anatomic region in 65 images.
When 20 images were re-read after 30 and 90 days, accuracy fell by up to 30%. Accuracy seemed unrelated to the model's self-reported confidence (Spearman's ρ = 0.117, p = 0.776).
key_points_pt: O GPT-4V leu 206 estudos imagiológicos com achados inequívocos (60 radiografias, 60 TC, 60 RM, 26 angiografias) duas vezes: apenas com a imagem e com contexto clínico e demográfico adicional.

A exatidão diagnóstica foi de 8,3% sem contexto, 29,1% com contexto (primeiro diagnóstico correto) e 63,6% com contexto (diagnóstico correto entre os diferenciais) (p ≤ 0,001). Os autores atribuem isto a uma tendência marcada para privilegiar o contexto em detrimento da informação da imagem.
O GPT-4V fabricou 258 achados imagiológicos em 412 respostas e identificou erradamente a modalidade de imagem ou a região anatómica em 65 imagens.
Na releitura de 20 imagens após 30 e 90 dias, a exatidão desceu até 30%. A exatidão pareceu não estar relacionada com a confiança autorreportada pelo modelo (ρ de Spearman = 0,117, p = 0,776).
abstract_excerpt: With its pronounced propensity to favor context over image information, the tool's diagnostic accuracy improved from 8.3% (uncontextualized) to 29.1% (contextualized, first diagnosis correct) and 63.6% (contextualized, correct diagnosis among differential diagnoses) (p ≤ 0.001, Cochran's Q test). Diagnostic accuracy declined by up to 30% when 20 images were re-read after 30 and 90 days and seemed unrelated to the tool's self-reported confidence (Spearman's ρ = 0.117 (p = 0.776)). While the described imaging findings matched the suggested diagnoses in 92.7%, indicating valid diagnostic reasoning, the tool fabricated 258 imaging findings in 412 responses and misidentified imaging modalities or anatomic regions in 65 images.

topic: Zero-shot multimodal LLMs (GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 1.5 Pro) vs CNN for pediatric wrist fracture detection
authors: Haupt M, Weiß D, Bellersen T, Maurer MH
title: Zero-shot multimodal large language models underperform a domain-trained CNN baseline in pediatric wrist fracture detection
key_points: GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet and Gemini 1.5 Pro were tested zero-shot for pediatric wrist fracture detection on a balanced GRAZPEDWRI-DX cohort of 1,000 children (2,298 radiographs; 500 fracture, 500 non-fracture).
A domain-trained Inception v3 CNN achieved AUROC 0.905 and AUPRC 0.920. All three multimodal LLMs performed close to chance (accuracies < 0.55, Matthews correlation coefficients ≈ 0).

The bounding boxes produced by the LLMs were often inconsistent with expert annotations. The authors regard these models as exploratory research tools, not clinically dependable systems for pediatric radiograph interpretation.
key_points_pt: O GPT-4o, o Claude 3.5 Sonnet e o Gemini 1.5 Pro foram testados em modo zero-shot na deteção de fraturas do punho em idade pediátrica, numa coorte equilibrada do GRAZPEDWRI-DX com 1000 crianças (2298 radiografias; 500 com fratura, 500 sem fratura).

Uma CNN Inception v3 treinada no domínio atingiu AUROC 0,905 e AUPRC 0,920. Os três modelos de linguagem multimodais tiveram um desempenho próximo do acaso (exatidão < 0,55, coeficiente de correlação de Matthews ≈ 0).

As caixas delimitadoras (bounding boxes) geradas pelos modelos de linguagem foram frequentemente inconsistentes com as anotações de especialistas. Os autores consideram estes modelos ferramentas de investigação exploratória, e não sistemas clinicamente fiáveis para a interpretação de radiografias pediátricas.
abstract_excerpt: We constructed a balanced patient-level test cohort of 1,000 children (2,298 radiographs; 500 fracture, 500 non-fracture). The CNN achieved high diagnostic performance (AUROC 0.905, AUPRC 0.920), whereas all LLMs performed close to chance (accuracies < 0.55, Matthews correlation coefficients ≈ 0) and produced bounding boxes often inconsistent with expert annotations. These findings indicate that, in a strict zero-shot setting, the three commercial multimodal LLMs evaluated here lack reliable diagnostic ability for pediatric wrist fracture detection and should therefore be regarded as exploratory research tools rather than clinically dependable systems for pediatric radiograph interpretation.

topic: General-purpose multimodal models on hip fracture radiographs: context sensitivity and overconfidence
authors: Gan-Or H, Ankol S, Ben Arie G, et al.
title: Between Accessibility and Reliability: High Confidence, Low Control in General-Purpose Multimodal Models for Hip Fracture Radiograph Interpretation
key_points: Behavioural characterization study of a fracture-positive cohort, explicitly not a diagnostic accuracy evaluation. It covered 214 surgically confirmed hip fractures on AP pelvis radiographs, read by two general-purpose multimodal models (GPT-5.4 and Gemini) under six prompting conditions. Because the cohort contained fractures only, detection rates are reported rather than full diagnostic-accuracy metrics (specificity cannot be estimated).
When the models were not told that a fracture was present, hip-fracture detection with correct laterality was 79.0% and 86.4% for GPT-5.4 and 80.4% and 93.5% for Gemini (runs E and F).
Incorrect laterality cues degraded performance from 90.7% to 66.4% (GPT-5.4) and from 97.7% to 57.0% (Gemini). AO/OTA grading and subtrochanteric identification remained limited.
Both models were often highly confident when wrong, and self-reported confidence did not reliably separate correct from incorrect outputs.
key_points_pt: Estudo de caracterização comportamental de uma coorte só com fraturas, explicitamente não uma avaliação de exatidão diagnóstica. Incluiu 214 fraturas da anca confirmadas cirurgicamente em radiografias AP da bacia, lidas por dois modelos multimodais de uso geral (GPT-5.4 e Gemini) em seis condições de prompt. Como a coorte só incluía fraturas, são reportadas taxas de deteção e não métricas completas de exatidão diagnóstica (a especificidade não pode ser estimada).
Quando os modelos não foram informados da presença de fratura, a deteção da fratura da anca com lateralidade correta foi de 79,0% e 86,4% no GPT-5.4 e de 80,4% e 93,5% no Gemini (séries E e F).

Pistas de lateralidade incorretas degradaram o desempenho de 90,7% para 66,4% (GPT-5.4) e de 97,7% para 57,0% (Gemini). A classificação AO/OTA e a identificação de fraturas subtrocantéricas mantiveram-se limitadas.
Ambos os modelos mostraram frequentemente confiança elevada quando erravam, e a confiança autorreportada não distinguiu de forma fiável as respostas corretas das incorretas.
abstract_excerpt: This was a behavioral characterization study of a fracture-positive cohort, not a diagnostic accuracy evaluation. ... Using the more conservative endpoint of hip-fracture detection with correct laterality, GPT-5.4 was correct in 79.0% and 86.4% of cases in runs E and F, whereas Gemini was correct in 80.4% and 93.5%, respectively. ... Incorrect laterality cues markedly degraded performance, from 90.7% to 66.4% in GPT-5.4 and from 97.7% to 57.0% in Gemini. Performance remained limited for treatment-relevant subtyping, particularly AO/OTA grading and subtrochanteric identification. Both models frequently remained highly confident when wrong, and self-reported confidence did not reliably distinguish correct from incorrect outputs.

topic: Meta-analysis: generative AI vs physicians in diagnostic radiology, effect of input modality
authors: Takita H, Kabata D, Walston SL, et al.
title: Generative AI versus physicians in diagnostic radiology: a systematic review and meta-analysis
key_points: PROSPERO-registered systematic review and meta-analysis (PRISMA-DTA) of 48 studies validating generative AI on diagnostic tasks in radiology (searches June 2018 to March 2025).
Pooled diagnostic accuracy of generative AI was 42.9% (95% CI, 35.8-50.1%) for free-text tasks and 58.1% (95% CI, 50.0-66.2%) for choice tasks.
Generative AI was significantly less accurate than expert physicians (physicians minus AI, +13.0 percentage points; 95% CI, 0.9-25.2; P = .038).

Text-only input was associated with higher accuracy than image-only input (image-only minus text-only, −25.9 percentage points; 95% CI, −39.1 to −12.8; P = .001) and than text-and-image input (−10.6 percentage points; 95% CI, −20.8 to −0.3; P = .046). The authors caution that this gap may reflect task difficulty and information content rather than input modality itself.
key_points_pt: Revisão sistemática e meta-análise registada no PROSPERO (PRISMA-DTA) de 48 estudos que validaram IA generativa em tarefas diagnósticas de radiologia (pesquisa de junho de 2018 a março de 2025).
A exatidão diagnóstica agregada da IA generativa foi de 42,9% (IC 95%, 35,8-50,1%) em tarefas de resposta livre e de 58,1% (IC 95%, 50,0-66,2%) em tarefas de escolha.
A IA generativa foi significativamente menos exata do que médicos especialistas (médicos menos IA: +13,0 pontos percentuais; IC 95%, 0,9-25,2; P = 0,038).

A entrada só de texto associou-se a maior exatidão do que a entrada só de imagem (só imagem menos só texto: −25,9 pontos percentuais; IC 95%, −39,1 a −12,8; P = 0,001) e do que a entrada de texto e imagem (−10,6 pontos percentuais; IC 95%, −20,8 a −0,3; P = 0,046). Os autores alertam que esta diferença pode refletir a dificuldade da tarefa e o conteúdo informativo, e não a modalidade de entrada em si.
keywords: modelo de linguagem de grande dimensão
abstract_excerpt: In total, 48 studies met inclusion criteria. Pooled diagnostic accuracy of generative AI was 42.9% (95% CI, 35.8-50.1%) for free-text tasks and 58.1% (95% CI, 50.0-66.2%) for choice tasks. Generative AI overall showed significantly lower accuracy than expert physicians (difference in accuracy [physicians minus AI], +13.0 percentage points [95% CI, 0.9-25.2]; P = .038). Text-only input was associated with higher accuracy than image-only input (difference in accuracy [image-only minus text-only], -25.9 percentage points [95% CI, -39.1 to -12.8]; P = .001) and text-and-image input (- 10.6 percentage points [95% CI, -20.8 to -0.3]; P = .046). ... the observed accuracy difference may reflect task difficulty and information content rather than the input modality itself.

topic: RadFM: generalist radiology foundation model for 2D and 3D scans
authors: Wu C, Zhang X, Zhang Y, et al.
title: Towards generalist foundation model for radiology by leveraging web-scale 2D&3D medical data
key_points: RadFM is a proof-of-concept generalist radiology foundation model whose architecture integrates text input with 2D or 3D medical scans.
The authors contributed 4 multimodal datasets with 13M 2D images and 615K 3D scans. Combined with existing datasets, these form the training set MedMD.

RadFM generates responses for diagnosis, visual question answering, report generation and rationale diagnosis. On the new RadBench benchmark (automatic and human evaluation), it outperformed earlier accessible multimodal foundation models, including GPT-4V. This is a benchmark evaluation, not clinical validation.
key_points_pt: O RadFM é um modelo de base (foundation model) generalista para radiologia, apresentado como prova de conceito, cuja arquitetura integra texto com exames médicos 2D ou 3D.
Os autores contribuíram com 4 conjuntos de dados multimodais com 13 milhões de imagens 2D e 615 mil exames 3D. Combinados com conjuntos já existentes, formam o conjunto de treino MedMD.

O RadFM gera respostas para diagnóstico, resposta a perguntas visuais, geração de relatórios e diagnóstico fundamentado. No novo benchmark RadBench (avaliação automática e humana), superou modelos de base multimodais acessíveis anteriores, incluindo o GPT-4V. Trata-se de uma avaliação em benchmark, não de validação clínica.
abstract_excerpt: In this study, as a proof-of-concept, we aim to initiate the development of Radiology Foundation Model, termed as RadFM. ... (i), we contribute 4 multimodal datasets with 13M 2D images and 615K 3D scans. When combined with a vast collection of existing datasets, this forms our training dataset, termed as Medical Multi-modal Dataset, MedMD. (ii), we propose an architecture that enables to integrate text input with 2D or 3D medical scans, and generates responses for diverse radiologic tasks, including diagnosis, visual question answering, report generation, and rationale diagnosis; ... We conduct both automatic and human evaluations on RadBench. RadFM outperforms former accessible multi-modal foundation models, including GPT-4V.

topic: LLaVA-Med: biomedical vision-language conversational assistant
authors: Li C, Wong C, Zhang S, et al.
title: LLaVA-Med: Training a Large Language-and-Vision Assistant for Biomedicine in One Day
journal: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 36 (NeurIPS 2023)
key_points: Peer-reviewed conference paper (NeurIPS 2023, proceedings pp. 28541-28564), verified via Crossref; not indexed in PubMed. The abstract is taken from arXiv 2306.00890.

LLaVA-Med is a biomedical vision-language conversational assistant. It was trained in under 15 hours on eight A100s, using a large PubMed Central figure-caption dataset, GPT-4 self-instructed instruction-following data and curriculum learning.

On three standard biomedical visual question answering datasets, it outperformed the previous supervised state of the art on certain metrics. This is a benchmark evaluation, not a clinical validation.
key_points_pt: Artigo de conferência com revisão por pares (NeurIPS 2023, atas pp. 28541-28564), verificado na Crossref; não está indexado na PubMed. O resumo foi obtido do arXiv 2306.00890.

O LLaVA-Med é um assistente conversacional biomédico de visão-linguagem. Foi treinado em menos de 15 horas com oito GPUs A100, usando um grande conjunto de pares figura-legenda da PubMed Central, dados de instruções autogerados pelo GPT-4 e aprendizagem curricular.

Em três conjuntos de dados padrão de resposta a perguntas visuais biomédicas, superou o estado da arte supervisionado anterior em algumas métricas. Trata-se de uma avaliação em benchmarks, não de uma validação clínica.
abstract_excerpt: The key idea is to leverage a large-scale, broad-coverage biomedical figure-caption dataset extracted from PubMed Central, use GPT-4 to self-instruct open-ended instruction-following data from the captions, and then fine-tune a large general-domain vision-language model using a novel curriculum learning method. ... This enables us to train a Large Language and Vision Assistant for BioMedicine (LLaVA-Med) in less than 15 hours (with eight A100s). LLaVA-Med exhibits excellent multimodal conversational capability and can follow open-ended instruction to assist with inquiries about a biomedical image. On three standard biomedical visual question answering datasets, LLaVA-Med outperforms previous supervised state-of-the-art on certain metrics.

topic: MedGemma: open medical vision-language foundation models (Gemma 3 based)
authors: Sellergren A, Kazemzadeh S, Mahvar F, et al.
title: An open vision-language model for diverse medical applications
key_points: Peer-reviewed publication (Nature Medicine, 2026) of the work first released as the MedGemma Technical Report preprint (arXiv 2507.05201). MedGemma is a collection of open medical vision-language foundation models based on Gemma 3, developed by Google.
On out-of-distribution tasks, MedGemma improved on the base models by 2.6-10% in medical image question answering, 15.5-18.1% in chest X-ray finding classification and 10.8% in agentic evaluations.
Fine-tuning MedGemma can be more effective than fine-tuning the base Gemma 3 model for medical tasks, particularly when training data are limited.

The collection includes MedSigLIP, a medically tuned vision encoder derived from SigLIP, which performed comparably to or better than many specialized medical image encoders. Results are developer-reported benchmark evaluations (nearly all authors are current or former Google employees), not clinical validation.
key_points_pt: Publicação com revisão por pares (Nature Medicine, 2026) do trabalho divulgado inicialmente como pré-publicação (MedGemma Technical Report, arXiv 2507.05201). O MedGemma é uma coleção de modelos de base de visão-linguagem médicos abertos, baseados no Gemma 3 e desenvolvidos pela Google.

Em tarefas fora da distribuição, o MedGemma superou os modelos base em 2,6-10% na resposta a perguntas sobre imagens médicas, 15,5-18,1% na classificação de achados em radiografia de tórax e 10,8% em avaliações agênticas.
A afinação (fine-tuning) do MedGemma pode ser mais eficaz do que a do modelo base Gemma 3 em tarefas médicas, sobretudo quando os dados de treino são limitados.

A coleção inclui o MedSigLIP, um codificador de visão adaptado à medicina e derivado do SigLIP, com desempenho comparável ou superior ao de muitos codificadores especializados de imagem médica. Os resultados são avaliações em benchmarks reportadas pelos criadores (quase todos os autores são ou foram funcionários da Google), não validação clínica.
abstract_excerpt: We introduce MedGemma, a collection of medical vision-language foundation models based on Gemma 3. MedGemma demonstrates advanced medical understanding and reasoning across images and text and multiple medical imaging domains, exceeding the performance of similarly sized generative models while maintaining the general capabilities of the Gemma base models. For out-of-distribution tasks, MedGemma achieves improvements of 2.6-10% in medical image question answering, 15.5-18.1% in chest X-ray finding classification and 10.8% in agentic evaluations compared with the base models. Our results show that fine-tuning MedGemma can be more effective than fine-tuning the base Gemma 3 model for medical tasks, particularly in the setting of limited training data. We additionally introduce MedSigLIP, a medically tuned vision encoder derived from SigLIP. MedSigLIP powers the visual understanding capabilities of MedGemma and, as an encoder, achieves performance comparable to or better than that of many specialized medical image encoders.

topic: Expert evaluation of VLM-generated radiology reports and clinician-AI collaboration
authors: Tanno R, Barrett DGT, Sellergren A, et al.
title: Collaboration between clinicians and vision-language models in radiology report generation
key_points: Flamingo-CXR, a chest radiograph report generation system, was evaluated by a panel of board-certified radiologists, whose preferences varied widely across the panel and clinical settings.

Half or more of the panel rated 56.1% of the intensive care reports as preferable or equivalent to clinician reports. This rose to 77.7% for in/outpatient X-rays and 94% for cases with no pertinent abnormal findings.
Among in/outpatient cases, 24.8% had clinically significant errors in both report types, 22.8% in Flamingo-CXR reports only and 14.0% in human reports only.
For reports containing errors, the authors demonstrated an assistive setting for clinician-AI collaboration in report composition.
key_points_pt: O Flamingo-CXR, um sistema de geração de relatórios de radiografia de tórax, foi avaliado por um painel de radiologistas certificados, cujas preferências variaram muito entre membros do painel e contextos clínicos.

Metade ou mais do painel considerou 56,1% dos relatórios de cuidados intensivos preferíveis ou equivalentes aos relatórios dos clínicos. A proporção subiu para 77,7% nas radiografias de internamento/ambulatório e para 94% nos casos sem achados anómalos relevantes.
Nos casos de internamento/ambulatório, 24,8% tinham erros clinicamente significativos em ambos os tipos de relatório, 22,8% apenas no relatório do Flamingo-CXR e 14,0% apenas no relatório humano.
Para os relatórios com erros, os autores demonstraram um modo assistivo de colaboração clínico-IA na redação do relatório.
abstract_excerpt: We observe a wide distribution of preferences across the panel and across clinical settings, with 56.1% of Flamingo-CXR intensive care reports evaluated to be preferable or equivalent to clinician reports, by half or more of the panel, rising to 77.7% for in/outpatient X-rays overall and to 94% for the subset of cases with no pertinent abnormal findings. Errors were observed in human-written reports and Flamingo-CXR reports, with 24.8% of in/outpatient cases containing clinically significant errors in both report types, 22.8% in Flamingo-CXR reports only and 14.0% in human reports only. For reports that contain errors we develop an assistive setting, a demonstration of clinician-AI collaboration for radiology report composition, indicating new possibilities for potential clinical utility.

topic: Automation bias: effect of incorrect AI suggestions on radiologist performance
authors: Dratsch T, Chen X, Rezazade Mehrizi M, et al.
title: Automation Bias in Mammography: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence BI-RADS Suggestions on Reader Performance
key_points: Prospective experiment in which 27 radiologists read 50 mammograms assisted by a purported AI system. In the 40-mammogram test set, the AI suggested an incorrect BI-RADS category for 12 mammograms.

The mean percentage of correctly rated mammograms fell when the AI suggestion was incorrect: from 79.7% to 19.8% for inexperienced, 81.3% to 24.8% for moderately experienced and 82.3% to 45.5% for very experienced radiologists (P < .001, P < .001, P = .003).

Inexperienced readers were more likely to follow incorrect suggestions of a higher BI-RADS category (mean degree of bias 4.0, versus 2.4 for moderately experienced, P = .044, and 1.2 for very experienced readers, P = .009).

Radiologists of all experience levels were prone to automation bias, and the authors state that human-AI interaction effects must be considered for safe deployment. The evidence comes from mammography (BI-RADS); applying it to AI-drafted MSK reports is an extrapolation not tested in this study.
key_points_pt: Experiência prospetiva em que 27 radiologistas leram 50 mamografias com o apoio de um suposto sistema de IA. No conjunto de teste de 40 mamografias, a IA sugeriu uma categoria BI-RADS incorreta em 12.

A percentagem média de mamografias corretamente classificadas desceu quando a sugestão da IA estava errada: de 79,7% para 19,8% nos inexperientes, de 81,3% para 24,8% nos moderadamente experientes e de 82,3% para 45,5% nos muito experientes (P < 0,001, P < 0,001, P = 0,003).

Os leitores inexperientes foram mais propensos a seguir sugestões incorretas de categoria BI-RADS superior (grau médio de viés 4,0, face a 2,4 nos moderadamente experientes, P = 0,044, e 1,2 nos muito experientes, P = 0,009).

Radiologistas de todos os níveis de experiência foram suscetíveis ao viés de automação, e os autores afirmam que os efeitos da interação humano-IA devem ser considerados para uma implementação segura. A evidência provém da mamografia (BI-RADS); a sua aplicação a relatórios musculoesqueléticos redigidos por IA é uma extrapolação não testada neste estudo.
abstract_excerpt: The percentage of correctly rated mammograms by inexperienced (mean, 79.7% ± 11.7 [SD] vs 19.8% ± 14.0; P < .001; r = 0.93), moderately experienced (mean, 81.3% ± 10.1 vs 24.8% ± 11.6; P < .001; r = 0.96), and very experienced (mean, 82.3% ± 4.2 vs 45.5% ± 9.1; P = .003; r = 0.97) radiologists was significantly impacted by the correctness of the AI prediction of BI-RADS category. Inexperienced radiologists were significantly more likely to follow the suggestions of the purported AI when it incorrectly suggested a higher BI-RADS category than the actual ground truth compared with both moderately (mean degree of bias, 4.0 ± 1.8 vs 2.4 ± 1.5; P = .044; r = 0.46) and very (mean degree of bias, 4.0 ± 1.8 vs 1.2 ± 0.8; P = .009; r = 0.65) experienced readers. Conclusion The results show that inexperienced, moderately experienced, and very experienced radiologists reading mammograms are prone to automation bias when being supported by an AI-based system.

topic: ESR position on structured reporting in radiology
title: ESR paper on structured reporting in radiology
key_points: The ESR endorses the move from conventional prose reports to structured reporting as a positive development, and says it must be an international effort.
Standardising the report structure ensures that reports are complete and comparable. Standardised language minimises ambiguity.

Structured reports that use key data elements and quantified parameters support automatic functions (e.g. TNM staging), integration with other clinical parameters, data sharing (registries, biobanks) and data mining.
A successful strategy requires defined content and structure, standard terminologies, tools and protocols, together with international and inter-society cooperation and integration with industry.
key_points_pt: A ESR endossa a transição dos relatórios convencionais em prosa para o relatório estruturado como um desenvolvimento positivo, que deve ser um esforço internacional.
A padronização da estrutura do relatório assegura que os relatórios são completos e comparáveis. A linguagem padronizada minimiza a ambiguidade.

Os relatórios estruturados com elementos de dados-chave e parâmetros quantificados suportam funções automáticas (p. ex., estadiamento TNM), a integração com outros parâmetros clínicos, a partilha de dados (registos, biobancos) e a mineração de dados.
Uma estratégia bem-sucedida requer conteúdo e estrutura definidos, terminologias padronizadas, ferramentas e protocolos, com cooperação internacional e entre sociedades e integração com a indústria.
abstract_excerpt: Standardisation of report structures ensures that all relevant areas are addressed. Standardisation of terminology prevents ambiguity in reports and facilitates comparability of reports. ... Moving from conventional prose reports to structured reporting is endorsed as a positive development, and must be an international effort, with international design and adoption of structured reporting templates that can be translated and adapted in local environments as needed. ... KEY POINTS: • Standardisation of radiology report structure ensures completeness and comparability of reports. • Use of standardised language in reports minimises ambiguity. • Structured reporting facilitates automatic functions, integration with other clinical parameters and data sharing.

topic: CLAIM reporting checklist for AI in medical imaging (original)
authors: Mongan J, Moy L, Kahn CE Jr
title: Checklist for Artificial Intelligence in Medical Imaging (CLAIM): A Guide for Authors and Reviewers
key_points: PubMed has no abstract for this paper; these points come from the full text (PMC8017414). CLAIM is a reporting checklist (items numbered 1-42) for authors and reviewers of manuscripts on AI in medical imaging.

CLAIM is modeled after the STARD guideline and extended to AI applications in medical imaging, including classification, image reconstruction, text analysis and workflow optimization. Its elements should be viewed as a 'best practice' to guide authors.
Its goal is to promote clear, transparent and reproducible scientific communication about the application of AI to medical imaging.
key_points_pt: A PubMed não tem resumo deste artigo; estes pontos foram retirados do texto integral (PMC8017414). O CLAIM é uma lista de verificação (itens numerados de 1 a 42) para autores e revisores de manuscritos sobre IA em imagiologia médica.

O CLAIM baseia-se na norma STARD e foi alargado às aplicações de IA em imagiologia médica, incluindo classificação, reconstrução de imagem, análise de texto e otimização do fluxo de trabalho. Os seus elementos devem ser vistos como 'boa prática' para orientar os autores.
O objetivo é promover uma comunicação científica clara, transparente e reprodutível sobre a aplicação de IA à imagiologia médica.
abstract_excerpt: [No PubMed abstract; quoted from the full text] To aid authors and reviewers of AI manuscripts in medical imaging, we propose CLAIM, the Checklist for AI in Medical Imaging ... CLAIM is modeled after the STARD guideline and has been extended to address applications of AI in medical imaging that include classification, image reconstruction, text analysis, and workflow optimization. The elements described here should be viewed as a “best practice” to guide authors in presenting their research.

topic: CLAIM 2024 update: reporting checklist for AI in medical imaging
authors: Tejani AS, Klontzas ME, Gatti AA, et al.
title: Checklist for Artificial Intelligence in Medical Imaging (CLAIM): 2024 Update
key_points: The CLAIM 2024 Update revises the checklist to keep pace with the rapid evolution of AI in medical imaging.
From the full text: the term 'reference standard' replaces 'ground truth', and each CLAIM item now has three options (Yes, No, Not Applicable).
From the full text: authors are encouraged to use 'internal testing' and 'external testing' rather than the ambiguous term 'validation'.
key_points_pt: A atualização CLAIM 2024 revê a lista de verificação para acompanhar a rápida evolução da IA em imagiologia médica.
Do texto integral: o termo 'padrão de referência' (reference standard) substitui 'ground truth', e cada item do CLAIM passa a ter três opções (Sim, Não, Não Aplicável).
Do texto integral: recomenda-se aos autores que usem 'teste interno' e 'teste externo' em vez do termo ambíguo 'validação'.
abstract_excerpt: To address the rapid evolution of artificial intelligence in medical imaging, the authors present the Checklist for Artificial Intelligence in Medical Imaging (CLAIM) 2024 Update. [Full text:] Each CLAIM item now has three options: Yes, No, and Not Applicable (NA). ... The term “reference standard” has been adopted in lieu of “ground truth.”

topic: Standardized lexicon for the radiologist's level of diagnostic certainty
title: How Sure Are You, Doctor? A Standardized Lexicon to Describe the Radiologist's Level of Certainty
key_points: A standardized lexicon for the radiologist's level of certainty can cut down the confusingly large number of words and phrases used to express diagnostic certainty.
Such a lexicon can minimize ambiguity and support clearer communication among radiologists, referring physicians and patients.

The authors share their experience with a lexicon they developed in 2009; for ease of communication, the lexicon itself is included in each of their radiology reports. The abstract reports no quantitative outcomes.
key_points_pt: Um léxico padronizado para o nível de certeza do radiologista pode reduzir o número confusamente elevado de palavras e expressões usadas para exprimir a certeza diagnóstica.
Esse léxico pode minimizar a ambiguidade e apoiar uma comunicação mais clara entre radiologistas, médicos requisitantes e doentes.
