Os autores partilham a experiência com um léxico que desenvolveram em 2009; para facilitar a comunicação, o próprio léxico é incluído em cada um dos seus relatórios radiológicos. O resumo não apresenta resultados quantitativos.
abstract_excerpt: OBJECTIVE: A standardized lexicon to specify the radiologist's level of certainty in a radiologic diagnosis can decrease the confusingly large number of words and phrases currently used for that purpose. Such a lexicon furthermore can minimize ambiguity and facilitate clearer communication among radiologists, referring physicians, and patients. CONCLUSION: We would like to share our experience with the lexicon that we developed in 2009. For ease of communication, the lexicon itself is included in each radiology report.

topic: Variability in phrases conveying diagnostic certainty in radiology reports
authors: Shinagare AB, Lacson R, Boland GW, et al.
title: Radiologist Preferences, Agreement, and Variability in Phrases Used to Convey Diagnostic Certainty in Radiology Reports
journal: Journal of the American College of Radiology
key_points: 239 radiologists at a tertiary academic hospital were surveyed on their preferred phrases for six categories of diagnostic certainty; 59.4% (142/239) responded.

Most preferred phrases: 'consistent with' (45.1%) for 100% confident; 'highly suggestive of' (46.5%) for very high likelihood; 'most likely' (31.0%) for high; 'may represent' (50.7%) for intermediate; 'unlikely' (47.2%) for low; 'very unlikely' (40.1%) for very low likelihood.

Krippendorff's α was 0.217, meaning radiologists do not consistently use the same phrases for similar degrees of confidence. The authors suggest that interventions to improve consistency may reduce ambiguity.
key_points_pt: Foram inquiridos 239 radiologistas de um hospital académico terciário sobre as expressões preferidas para seis categorias de certeza diagnóstica; responderam 59,4% (142/239).

Expressões preferidas: 'consistent with' (compatível com; 45,1%) para 100% de certeza; 'highly suggestive of' (altamente sugestivo de; 46,5%) para probabilidade muito alta; 'most likely' (muito provavelmente; 31,0%) para alta; 'may represent' (pode representar; 50,7%) para intermédia; 'unlikely' (improvável; 47,2%) para baixa; 'very unlikely' (muito improvável; 40,1%) para muito baixa.

O α de Krippendorff foi de 0,217, o que significa que os radiologistas não usam de forma consistente as mesmas expressões para graus de confiança semelhantes. Os autores sugerem que intervenções para melhorar a consistência podem reduzir a ambiguidade.
abstract_excerpt: In all, 59.4% (142 of 239) of radiologists completed the survey. The most commonly preferred phrases were "consistent with" (45.1%; 64 of 142) for 100% confident, "highly suggestive of" (46.5%; 66 of 142) for very high likelihood, "most likely" (31.0%; 44 of 142) for high likelihood, "may represent" (50.7%; 72 of 142) for intermediate likelihood, "unlikely" (47.2%; 67 of 142) for low likelihood, and "very unlikely" (40.1%; 57 of 142) for very low likelihood. Cluster analysis identified six groups of phrases used to indicate a similar level of diagnostic certainty; however, Krippendorff's α was 0.217, indicating radiologists do not consistently use the same phrases for similar degrees of confidence.

topic: ESR recommendations for implementing the EU AI Act in medical imaging
authors: Kotter E, D'Antonoli TA, Cuocolo R, et al.
title: Guiding AI in radiology: ESR's recommendations for effective implementation of the European AI Act
key_points: Statement from the European Society of Radiology AI Working Group that identifies the key EU AI Act policies for medical imaging and gives recommendations to policymakers and the professional community.

Key areas: AI literacy, classification rules for high-risk AI systems, data governance, transparency, human oversight, quality management, deployer obligations, regulatory sandboxes, post-market monitoring, information sharing and market surveillance.
The AI Act will significantly affect medical imaging, shaping how AI technologies are used and regulated.
key_points_pt: Declaração do Grupo de Trabalho de IA da Sociedade Europeia de Radiologia que identifica as principais disposições do Regulamento Europeu da Inteligência Artificial (AI Act) para a imagiologia médica e dá recomendações a decisores políticos e profissionais.

Áreas-chave: literacia em IA, regras de classificação de sistemas de IA de risco elevado, governação de dados, transparência, supervisão humana, gestão da qualidade, obrigações dos responsáveis pela implantação, ambientes de testagem da regulamentação (sandboxes), acompanhamento pós-comercialização, partilha de informação e fiscalização do mercado.
O AI Act terá um impacto significativo na imagiologia médica, moldando a forma como as tecnologias de IA são usadas e reguladas.

abstract_excerpt: This statement has been produced within the European Society of Radiology AI Working Group and identifies the key policies of the EU AI Act as they pertain to medical imaging. It offers specific recommendations to policymakers and the professional community for the effective implementation of the legislation, addressing potential gaps and uncertainties. Key areas include AI literacy, classification rules for high-risk AI systems, data governance, transparency, human oversight, quality management, deployer obligations, regulatory sandboxes, post-market monitoring, information sharing, and market surveillance. ... The AI Act will significantly impact the field of medical imaging, shaping how AI technologies are used and regulated.

topic: ESR consensus on post-market surveillance of AI medical devices under MDR and the AI Act
authors: Cuocolo R, Bernardini D, Pinto Dos Santos D, et al.
title: AI medical device post-market surveillance regulations: consensus recommendations by the European Society of Radiology
key_points: ESR consensus from a modified Delphi procedure with 16 domain experts, 14 of whom acted as panelists. It sets practices for post-market surveillance (PMS) and post-market clinical feedback (PMCF) of AI as a medical device (AIaMD), as required by the EU MDR and partly updated by the AI Act.

According to the authors, neither the MDR nor the EU AI Act contains explicit provisions tailored to AI components, and a significant awareness gap about these regulations persists among radiologists.
Legal responsibility for AIaMD post-market surveillance rests mainly with software providers, but radiologists, as deployers, are expected to help monitor safety and performance.
key_points_pt: Consenso da ESR obtido por procedimento Delphi modificado com 16 peritos, dos quais 14 atuaram como painelistas. Estabelece práticas de vigilância pós-comercialização (PMS) e de feedback clínico pós-comercialização (PMCF) de IA como dispositivo médico (AIaMD), exigidas pelo Regulamento de Dispositivos Médicos (MDR) e parcialmente atualizadas pelo AI Act.
Segundo os autores, nem o MDR nem o AI Act contêm disposições explícitas adaptadas a componentes de IA, e persiste entre os radiologistas uma lacuna significativa no conhecimento destes regulamentos.

A responsabilidade legal pela vigilância pós-comercialização recai sobretudo sobre os fornecedores do software, mas espera-se que os radiologistas, enquanto responsáveis pela implantação, ajudem a monitorizar a segurança e o desempenho.
abstract_excerpt: Despite the growing commercial availability and adoption of AIaMD, a significant awareness gap persists among radiologists regarding pertinent European Union regulations, including the Medical Device Regulation (MDR) and the novel EU AI Act, both of which lack explicit provisions tailored to AI components. ... Legal responsibility for AIaMD Post-Market Surveillance (PMS) primarily rests with software providers, yet radiologists are expected to contribute to the ongoing monitoring of safety and performance. Recognizing the need to raise awareness and provide practical guidance, the European Society of Radiology (ESR) eHealth and Informatics Subcommittee, supported by the ESR AI Working Group, conducted a modified Delphi procedure involving 16 domain experts (of which 14 acted as panelists) to establish a set of shared recommendations.

topic: Context-based (retrieval-grounded) LLM chatbot using ACR Appropriateness Criteria
authors: Rau A, Rau S, Zoeller D, et al.
title: A Context-based Chatbot Surpasses Trained Radiologists and Generic ChatGPT in Following the ACR Appropriateness Guidelines
key_points: accGPT connected GPT-3.5-Turbo through LlamaIndex to a specialized knowledge base of 209 ACR Appropriateness Criteria documents, using semantic similarity processing. On 50 clinical case files it was compared with generic ChatGPT 3.5 and 4.0 and with general radiologists of varying experience.
All chatbots reached at least human performance. accGPT performed best at giving recommendations rated 'usually appropriate' and had the highest proportion of consistently correct answers.
For all cases, the chatbots took an average of 5 minutes and cost €0.19, versus 50 minutes and €29.99 for radiologists (both p < 0.01).
The study assessed imaging-recommendation decisions, not image interpretation. The context-based algorithm outperformed its generic counterpart.
key_points_pt: O accGPT ligou o GPT-3.5-Turbo, através do LlamaIndex, a uma base de conhecimento especializada de 209 documentos dos Critérios de Adequação do ACR, com processamento de semelhança semântica. Em 50 casos clínicos, foi comparado com o ChatGPT 3.5 e 4.0 genéricos e com radiologistas gerais com diferentes níveis de experiência.

Todos os chatbots atingiram pelo menos o nível de desempenho humano. O accGPT foi o melhor a dar recomendações classificadas como 'usually appropriate' e teve a maior proporção de respostas consistentemente corretas.
No conjunto dos casos, os chatbots demoraram em média 5 minutos e custaram 0,19 €, face a 50 minutos e 29,99 € para os radiologistas (ambos p < 0,01).
O estudo avaliou decisões de recomendação de exames, não a interpretação de imagens. O algoritmo baseado em contexto superou o equivalente genérico.
abstract_excerpt: Methods We utilized 209 ACR appropriateness criteria documents as specialized knowledge base and employed LlamaIndex, a framework that allows to connect large language models with external data, and the ChatGPT 3.5-Turbo to create an appropriateness criteria contexted chatbot (accGPT). ... Results All chatbots reached at least human performance level. For the 50 case files, the accGPT performed best in providing correct recommendations that were "usually appropriate" according to the ACR criteria and also did provide the highest proportion of consistently correct answers in comparison with generic chatbots and radiologists. Further, the chatbots provided substantial time and cost savings, with an average decision time of 5 minutes and a cost of 0.19 € for all cases, compared to 50 minutes and 29.99 € for radiologists (both p < 0.01).

topic: Online retrieval-augmented generation (RadioRAG) for radiology question answering
authors: Tayebi Arasteh S, Lotfinia M, Bressem K, et al.
title: RadioRAG: Online Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Radiology Question Answering
key_points: RadioRAG retrieves context-specific information in real time from authoritative online radiology sources (www.radiopaedia.org) to ground LLM answers. It was tested on 80 RSNA Case Collection questions and 24 expert-curated questions.
Accuracy improved for some LLMs, e.g. GPT-3.5-turbo 74% (59/80) vs 66% (53/80), FDR = 0.03, and Mixtral 8×7B 76% (61/80) vs 65% (52/80), FDR = 0.02. Not every model benefited.
RadioRAG reduced hallucinations for all LLMs (rate, 6%-25%) but made the estimated response time four times longer.
key_points_pt: O RadioRAG obtém em tempo real informação contextual de fontes radiológicas online de referência (www.radiopaedia.org) para fundamentar as respostas dos modelos de linguagem. Foi testado em 80 perguntas da RSNA Case Collection e em 24 perguntas selecionadas por especialistas.
A exatidão melhorou em alguns modelos, p. ex. GPT-3.5-turbo 74% (59/80) vs. 66% (53/80), FDR = 0,03, e Mixtral 8×7B 76% (61/80) vs. 65% (52/80), FDR = 0,02. Nem todos os modelos beneficiaram.
O RadioRAG reduziu as alucinações em todos os modelos (taxa, 6%-25%), mas tornou o tempo de resposta estimado quatro vezes mais longo.
keywords: modelo de linguagem de grande dimensão
abstract_excerpt: Results RadioRAG improved accuracy for some LLMs, including GPT-3.5-turbo (74% [59 of 80] vs 66% [53 of 80], false discovery rate [FDR] = 0.03) and Mixtral 8×7B (76% [61 of 80] vs 65% [52 of 80], FDR = 0.02) on the RSNA radiology question answering (RSNA-RadioQA) dataset, with similar trends in the ExtendedQA dataset. ... RadioRAG reduced hallucinations for all LLMs (rate, 6%-25%). RadioRAG increased estimated response time fourfold. Conclusion RadioRAG shows potential to improve LLM accuracy and factuality in radiology QA by integrating real-time, domain-specific data.
